# gh-1555: [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop; legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable

## Description

## Goal — unbounded session JSONL growth defeats the 2 GiB full-open backstop (v1, initial draft)

One sentence: **every session remains openable forever at ANY size — 100 GB included — through lazy, tail-first, bounded-memory reads, and no ledger record is ever lost**: size is a read-pattern problem, never a deletion problem.

Today a session JSONL is append-only forever: compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file, and nothing rotates or trims by size. The gh-1073 backstop (`defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30`, lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30) converted the old silent heap explosion into a loud `SessionException` refusal — but nothing on the write side slows growth and nothing on the read side migrates the legacy full-open call sites to the existing windowed reader. So every active named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. This happened in production on 2026-10-11 (incident below). This card changes both sides: all tail/preview/trajectory read paths migrate to windowed/token-budgeted opens, and the ledger gains a size-based rotation/trim plus write-side caps on the dominant growth drivers.

## Owner directive (2026-10-11, supersedes any size-budget thinking below)

- **Sessions are never lost.** Not by trim, not by rotation, not by repair, not by write-side cap applied retroactively. A 100 GB ledger is a valid ledger. Any solution whose size story involves deleting or truncating EXISTING records is rejected by definition.
- **Openability is unconditional.** Picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — all must work on a 100 GB session with bounded memory. If a path cannot be made lazy, the path is buggy, not the session "too big".
- **Context-meter continuity across close/reopen.** A session closed showing 59% context usage reopens showing the same 59% — the resume boundary (newest compaction boundary, or the token-budget tail for a boundary-less marathon) must reconstruct EXACTLY the context the live loop carried at exit, not an approximation. Wrong boundary = wrong meter = a regression the owner can see.
- **Lazy loading everywhere, export included.** Today `exportTrajectoryJson`/`exportTrajectoryMarkdown` (lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:16,33) take a fully materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` — pure functions over `snapshot.records`, no IO. That means export transitively requires the full open it should avoid. Export must become scan-and-emit streaming: read records in bounded chunks, serialize incrementally to the sink, never materialize the snapshot.
- **Forward-looking write-side reduction** (W3) is permitted ONLY as opt-in and only for FUTURE records, and even then is an owner-call open question — never the mechanism that makes old sessions openable.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted framing 1:** "just raise/disable the 2 GiB bound" — the bound exists because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile (gh-1073); raising it re-opens the OOM. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 2:** "compaction alone fixes size" — compaction APPENDS a summary record; it never shrinks the file. The "network" incident session reached 2.54 GiB with **zero** compaction records; the ssh/followup session reached 2.91 GB **with** 51 compaction records. Compaction reduces model context, not bytes on disk. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 3:** "this is a read-side-only fix" — migrating call sites keeps the bomb ticking at 0.4–0.6 GB/week; the write side needs caps and a trim story. Retracted as insufficient (kept as the core tier, not the whole card).
- **Retracted framing 4:** "trim/rotate/delete old records to stay under a size budget" — owner directive 2026-10-11: the ledger is sacred, a 100 GB session must open, and no existing record may be lost. Rotation is allowed ONLY as split-and-retain (all `.part-NN` siblings kept and reassembled by the reader); repair keeps its `.bak` until the user explicitly removes it. Retracted.

## Incident (2026-10-11, all numbers measured with `stat -f %z` and `LC_ALL=C grep -c '"type":"compaction"'`)

The owner tried to open two sessions from the fa TUI session picker; both failed with `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session <path>: … exceeds the 2.0 GiB full-open bound`:

| Session | Created | Bytes | Size | Compaction records |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01a0d73f` ("network") | 2026-09-25 | 2,737,991,964 | 2.54 GiB | **0** in 2.7 GB of JSONL |
| `e7a689` (.worktrees/issue/355/ssh/followup) | 2026-09-14 | 2,912,096,469 | 2.91 GB | 51 |
| `01a06644` ("goal_builder") | 2026-09-03 | 2,236,083,302 | 2.08 GiB | 6 |

Sessions live under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/<slug>/`. Measured growth: ~0.4–0.6 GB/week on active named sessions.

## Mechanism chain (pinned facts — each verified against the working tree 2026-10-11)

- **(a) Append-only forever.** Session JSONL grows monotonically; compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file; nothing rotates or trims by size.
- **(b) Growth drivers.** Measured on goal_builder's last 500 MB (10,196 records): hidden `model_request_summary` custom records ≈ **0.7 MB EACH** (one per outbound LLM request — they persist a request-detail snapshot for the trajectory Request tab), plus multi-MB toolResult records (full test-run logs). Top records in the chunk: one 1.5 MB toolResult, then an unbroken run of 0.7 MB model_request_summary records.
- **(c) The windowed tail-reader EXISTS and is the intended design.** `WindowedSessionStorage.open` via `SessionRepo.open(metadata, windowed: true)` at lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:343 (doc comment: "the app's chat path, issue #135 … only the header plus the newest chunk are materialized"). The CLI resume `_loadSession` opens windowed (lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:582) and pages back only to the newest compaction boundary under a token budget (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`, gh-968 parity budget).
- **(d) BUT seven legacy call sites still take the DEFAULT full open (windowed:false):**
  1. lib/src/cli/agent_cli_pickers.dart:74 — TUI session picker `_tuiPickSession` does `_repo.open(metadata)`; the catch at :82 prints exactly the observed `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session …`. **← the user's exact failure path.**
  2. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:611 — `_loadSession` full-open FALLBACK when `ensureCompactionBoundaryResident` returns false (a marathon with NO compaction boundary). The "network" session has 0 compaction records → even the main resume path degenerates to full open → guaranteed refusal past 2 GiB.
  3. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:196 — `_resumeLastSession` full open.
  4. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:492 — name-resolution fallback loop, full-open PER SESSION until name match.
  5. lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:64,67,71 — `fa trajectory view/tail/cost/inspect` resolve via `repo.open(metadata)` full.
  6. bin/fah_trajectory.dart:94 — headless trajectory full open.
  7. lib/src/cli/agent_commands.dart:314 — `_openChildSession` (subagent transcript preview) full open.
- **(e) The backstop itself.** `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` (lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30); refusal thrown at :641 and :752 with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` (gh-1073 — added because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile).

The backstop converted a silent heap explosion into a loud refusal — but nothing on the WRITE side slows growth, and nothing on the READ side migrates the legacy call sites to windowed. content.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the

  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after

blocks.text:
# gh-1555: [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop; legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable

## Description

## Goal — unbounded session JSONL growth defeats the 2 GiB full-open backstop (v1, initial draft)

One sentence: **every session remains openable forever at ANY size — 100 GB included — through lazy, tail-first, bounded-memory reads, and no ledger record is ever lost**: size is a read-pattern problem, never a deletion problem.

Today a session JSONL is append-only forever: compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file, and nothing rotates or trims by size. The gh-1073 backstop (`defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30`, lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30) converted the old silent heap explosion into a loud `SessionException` refusal — but nothing on the write side slows growth and nothing on the read side migrates the legacy full-open call sites to the existing windowed reader. So every active named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. This happened in production on 2026-10-11 (incident below). This card changes both sides: all tail/preview/trajectory read paths migrate to windowed/token-budgeted opens, and the ledger gains a size-based rotation/trim plus write-side caps on the dominant growth drivers.

## Owner directive (2026-10-11, supersedes any size-budget thinking below)

- **Sessions are never lost.** Not by trim, not by rotation, not by repair, not by write-side cap applied retroactively. A 100 GB ledger is a valid ledger. Any solution whose size story involves deleting or truncating EXISTING records is rejected by definition.
- **Openability is unconditional.** Picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — all must work on a 100 GB session with bounded memory. If a path cannot be made lazy, the path is buggy, not the session "too big".
- **Context-meter continuity across close/reopen.** A session closed showing 59% context usage reopens showing the same 59% — the resume boundary (newest compaction boundary, or the token-budget tail for a boundary-less marathon) must reconstruct EXACTLY the context the live loop carried at exit, not an approximation. Wrong boundary = wrong meter = a regression the owner can see.
- **Lazy loading everywhere, export included.** Today `exportTrajectoryJson`/`exportTrajectoryMarkdown` (lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:16,33) take a fully materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` — pure functions over `snapshot.records`, no IO. That means export transitively requires the full open it should avoid. Export must become scan-and-emit streaming: read records in bounded chunks, serialize incrementally to the sink, never materialize the snapshot.
- **Forward-looking write-side reduction** (W3) is permitted ONLY as opt-in and only for FUTURE records, and even then is an owner-call open question — never the mechanism that makes old sessions openable.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted framing 1:** "just raise/disable the 2 GiB bound" — the bound exists because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile (gh-1073); raising it re-opens the OOM. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 2:** "compaction alone fixes size" — compaction APPENDS a summary record; it never shrinks the file. The "network" incident session reached 2.54 GiB with **zero** compaction records; the ssh/followup session reached 2.91 GB **with** 51 compaction records. Compaction reduces model context, not bytes on disk. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 3:** "this is a read-side-only fix" — migrating call sites keeps the bomb ticking at 0.4–0.6 GB/week; the write side needs caps and a trim story. Retracted as insufficient (kept as the core tier, not the whole card).
- **Retracted framing 4:** "trim/rotate/delete old records to stay under a size budget" — owner directive 2026-10-11: the ledger is sacred, a 100 GB session must open, and no existing record may be lost. Rotation is allowed ONLY as split-and-retain (all `.part-NN` siblings kept and reassembled by the reader); repair keeps its `.bak` until the user explicitly removes it. Retracted.

## Incident (2026-10-11, all numbers measured with `stat -f %z` and `LC_ALL=C grep -c '"type":"compaction"'`)

The owner tried to open two sessions from the fa TUI session picker; both failed with `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session <path>: … exceeds the 2.0 GiB full-open bound`:

| Session | Created | Bytes | Size | Compaction records |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01a0d73f` ("network") | 2026-09-25 | 2,737,991,964 | 2.54 GiB | **0** in 2.7 GB of JSONL |
| `e7a689` (.worktrees/issue/355/ssh/followup) | 2026-09-14 | 2,912,096,469 | 2.91 GB | 51 |
| `01a06644` ("goal_builder") | 2026-09-03 | 2,236,083,302 | 2.08 GiB | 6 |

Sessions live under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/<slug>/`. Measured growth: ~0.4–0.6 GB/week on active named sessions.

## Mechanism chain (pinned facts — each verified against the working tree 2026-10-11)

- **(a) Append-only forever.** Session JSONL grows monotonically; compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file; nothing rotates or trims by size.
- **(b) Growth drivers.** Measured on goal_builder's last 500 MB (10,196 records): hidden `model_request_summary` custom records ≈ **0.7 MB EACH** (one per outbound LLM request — they persist a request-detail snapshot for the trajectory Request tab), plus multi-MB toolResult records (full test-run logs). Top records in the chunk: one 1.5 MB toolResult, then an unbroken run of 0.7 MB model_request_summary records.
- **(c) The windowed tail-reader EXISTS and is the intended design.** `WindowedSessionStorage.open` via `SessionRepo.open(metadata, windowed: true)` at lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:343 (doc comment: "the app's chat path, issue #135 … only the header plus the newest chunk are materialized"). The CLI resume `_loadSession` opens windowed (lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:582) and pages back only to the newest compaction boundary under a token budget (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`, gh-968 parity budget).
- **(d) BUT seven legacy call sites still take the DEFAULT full open (windowed:false):**
  1. lib/src/cli/agent_cli_pickers.dart:74 — TUI session picker `_tuiPickSession` does `_repo.open(metadata)`; the catch at :82 prints exactly the observed `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session …`. **← the user's exact failure path.**
  2. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:611 — `_loadSession` full-open FALLBACK when `ensureCompactionBoundaryResident` returns false (a marathon with NO compaction boundary). The "network" session has 0 compaction records → even the main resume path degenerates to full open → guaranteed refusal past 2 GiB.
  3. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:196 — `_resumeLastSession` full open.
  4. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:492 — name-resolution fallback loop, full-open PER SESSION until name match.
  5. lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:64,67,71 — `fa trajectory view/tail/cost/inspect` resolve via `repo.open(metadata)` full.
  6. bin/fah_trajectory.dart:94 — headless trajectory full open.
  7. lib/src/cli/agent_commands.dart:314 — `_openChildSession` (subagent transcript preview) full open.
- **(e) The backstop itself.** `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` (lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30); refusal thrown at :641 and :752 with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` (gh-1073 — added because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile).

### Amplification

The backstop converted a silent heap explosion into a loud refusal — but nothing on the WRITE side slows growth, and nothing on the READ side migrates the legacy call sites to windowed. So every long-lived named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. The gh-1073 refusal message even prescribes `fa --session …` and `fa session repair` — both of which themselves degenerate to a refuse…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

# gh-1555: [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop; legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable

## Description

## Goal — unbounded session JSONL growth defeats the 2 GiB full-open backstop (v1, initial draft)

One sentence: **every session remains openable forever at ANY size — 100 GB included — through lazy, tail-first, bounded-memory reads, and no ledger record is ever lost**: size is a read-pattern problem, never a deletion problem.

Today a session JSONL is append-only forever: compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file, and nothing rotates or trims by size. The gh-1073 backstop (`defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30`, lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30) converted the old silent heap explosion into a loud `SessionException` refusal — but nothing on the write side slows growth and nothing on the read side migrates the legacy full-open call sites to the existing windowed reader. So every active named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. This happened in production on 2026-10-11 (incident below). This card changes both sides: all tail/preview/trajectory read paths migrate to windowed/token-budgeted opens, and the ledger gains a size-based rotation/trim plus write-side caps on the dominant growth drivers.

## Owner directive (2026-10-11, supersedes any size-budget thinking below)

- **Sessions are never lost.** Not by trim, not by rotation, not by repair, not by write-side cap applied retroactively. A 100 GB ledger is a valid ledger. Any solution whose size story involves deleting or truncating EXISTING records is rejected by definition.
- **Openability is unconditional.** Picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — all must work on a 100 GB session with bounded memory. If a path cannot be made lazy, the path is buggy, not the session "too big".
- **Context-meter continuity across close/reopen.** A session closed showing 59% context usage reopens showing the same 59% — the resume boundary (newest compaction boundary, or the token-budget tail for a boundary-less marathon) must reconstruct EXACTLY the context the live loop carried at exit, not an approximation. Wrong boundary = wrong meter = a regression the owner can see.
- **Lazy loading everywhere, export included.** Today `exportTrajectoryJson`/`exportTrajectoryMarkdown` (lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:16,33) take a fully materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` — pure functions over `snapshot.records`, no IO. That means export transitively requires the full open it should avoid. Export must become scan-and-emit streaming: read records in bounded chunks, serialize incrementally to the sink, never materialize the snapshot.
- **Forward-looking write-side reduction** (W3) is permitted ONLY as opt-in and only for FUTURE records, and even then is an owner-call open question — never the mechanism that makes old sessions openable.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted framing 1:** "just raise/disable the 2 GiB bound" — the bound exists because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile (gh-1073); raising it re-opens the OOM. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 2:** "compaction alone fixes size" — compaction APPENDS a summary record; it never shrinks the file. The "network" incident session reached 2.54 GiB with **zero** compaction records; the ssh/followup session reached 2.91 GB **with** 51 compaction records. Compaction reduces model context, not bytes on disk. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 3:** "this is a read-side-only fix" — migrating call sites keeps the bomb ticking at 0.4–0.6 GB/week; the write side needs caps and a trim story. Retracted as insufficient (kept as the core tier, not the whole card).
- **Retracted framing 4:** "trim/rotate/delete old records to stay under a size budget" — owner directive 2026-10-11: the ledger is sacred, a 100 GB session must open, and no existing record may be lost. Rotation is allowed ONLY as split-and-retain (all `.part-NN` siblings kept and reassembled by the reader); repair keeps its `.bak` until the user explicitly removes it. Retracted.

## Incident (2026-10-11, all numbers measured with `stat -f %z` and `LC_ALL=C grep -c '"type":"compaction"'`)

The owner tried to open two sessions from the fa TUI session picker; both failed with `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session <path>: … exceeds the 2.0 GiB full-open bound`:

| Session | Created | Bytes | Size | Compaction records |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01a0d73f` ("network") | 2026-09-25 | 2,737,991,964 | 2.54 GiB | **0** in 2.7 GB of JSONL |
| `e7a689` (.worktrees/issue/355/ssh/followup) | 2026-09-14 | 2,912,096,469 | 2.91 GB | 51 |
| `01a06644` ("goal_builder") | 2026-09-03 | 2,236,083,302 | 2.08 GiB | 6 |

Sessions live under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/<slug>/`. Measured growth: ~0.4–0.6 GB/week on active named sessions.

## Mechanism chain (pinned facts — each verified against the working tree 2026-10-11)

- **(a) Append-only forever.** Session JSONL grows monotonically; compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file; nothing rotates or trims by size.
- **(b) Growth drivers.** Measured on goal_builder's last 500 MB (10,196 records): hidden `model_request_summary` custom records ≈ **0.7 MB EACH** (one per outbound LLM request — they persist a request-detail snapshot for the trajectory Request tab), plus multi-MB toolResult records (full test-run logs). Top records in the chunk: one 1.5 MB toolResult, then an unbroken run of 0.7 MB model_request_summary records.
- **(c) The windowed tail-reader EXISTS and is the intended design.** `WindowedSessionStorage.open` via `SessionRepo.open(metadata, windowed: true)` at lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:343 (doc comment: "the app's chat path, issue #135 … only the header plus the newest chunk are materialized"). The CLI resume `_loadSession` opens windowed (lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:582) and pages back only to the newest compaction boundary under a token budget (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`, gh-968 parity budget).
- **(d) BUT seven legacy call sites still take the DEFAULT full open (windowed:false):**
  1. lib/src/cli/agent_cli_pickers.dart:74 — TUI session picker `_tuiPickSession` does `_repo.open(metadata)`; the catch at :82 prints exactly the observed `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session …`. **← the user's exact failure path.**
  2. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:611 — `_loadSession` full-open FALLBACK when `ensureCompactionBoundaryResident` returns false (a marathon with NO compaction boundary). The "network" session has 0 compaction records → even the main resume path degenerates to full open → guaranteed refusal past 2 GiB.
  3. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:196 — `_resumeLastSession` full open.
  4. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:492 — name-resolution fallback loop, full-open PER SESSION until name match.
  5. lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:64,67,71 — `fa trajectory view/tail/cost/inspect` resolve via `repo.open(metadata)` full.
  6. bin/fah_trajectory.dart:94 — headless trajectory full open.
  7. lib/src/cli/agent_commands.dart:314 — `_openChildSession` (subagent transcript preview) full open.
- **(e) The backstop itself.** `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` (lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30); refusal thrown at :641 and :752 with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` (gh-1073 — added because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile).

### Amplification

The backstop converted a silent heap explosion into a loud refusal — but nothing on the WRITE side slows growth, and nothing on the READ side migrates the legacy call sites to windowed. So every long-lived named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. The gh-1073 refusal message even prescribes `fa --session …` and `fa session repair` — both of which themselves degenerate to a refuse…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

# gh-1555: [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop; legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable

## Description

## Goal — unbounded session JSONL growth defeats the 2 GiB full-open backstop (v1, initial draft)

One sentence: **every session remains openable forever at ANY size — 100 GB included — through lazy, tail-first, bounded-memory reads, and no ledger record is ever lost**: size is a read-pattern problem, never a deletion problem.

Today a session JSONL is append-only forever: compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file, and nothing rotates or trims by size. The gh-1073 backstop (`defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30`, lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30) converted the old silent heap explosion into a loud `SessionException` refusal — but nothing on the write side slows growth and nothing on the read side migrates the legacy full-open call sites to the existing windowed reader. So every active named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. This happened in production on 2026-10-11 (incident below). This card changes both sides: all tail/preview/trajectory read paths migrate to windowed/token-budgeted opens, and the ledger gains a size-based rotation/trim plus write-side caps on the dominant growth drivers.

## Owner directive (2026-10-11, supersedes any size-budget thinking below)

- **Sessions are never lost.** Not by trim, not by rotation, not by repair, not by write-side cap applied retroactively. A 100 GB ledger is a valid ledger. Any solution whose size story involves deleting or truncating EXISTING records is rejected by definition.
- **Openability is unconditional.** Picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — all must work on a 100 GB session with bounded memory. If a path cannot be made lazy, the path is buggy, not the session "too big".
- **Context-meter continuity across close/reopen.** A session closed showing 59% context usage reopens showing the same 59% — the resume boundary (newest compaction boundary, or the token-budget tail for a boundary-less marathon) must reconstruct EXACTLY the context the live loop carried at exit, not an approximation. Wrong boundary = wrong meter = a regression the owner can see.
- **Lazy loading everywhere, export included.** Today `exportTrajectoryJson`/`exportTrajectoryMarkdown` (lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:16,33) take a fully materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` — pure functions over `snapshot.records`, no IO. That means export transitively requires the full open it should avoid. Export must become scan-and-emit streaming: read records in bounded chunks, serialize incrementally to the sink, never materialize the snapshot.
- **Forward-looking write-side reduction** (W3) is permitted ONLY as opt-in and only for FUTURE records, and even then is an owner-call open question — never the mechanism that makes old sessions openable.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted framing 1:** "just raise/disable the 2 GiB bound" — the bound exists because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile (gh-1073); raising it re-opens the OOM. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 2:** "compaction alone fixes size" — compaction APPENDS a summary record; it never shrinks the file. The "network" incident session reached 2.54 GiB with **zero** compaction records; the ssh/followup session reached 2.91 GB **with** 51 compaction records. Compaction reduces model context, not bytes on disk. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 3:** "this is a read-side-only fix" — migrating call sites keeps the bomb ticking at 0.4–0.6 GB/week; the write side needs caps and a trim story. Retracted as insufficient (kept as the core tier, not the whole card).
- **Retracted framing 4:** "trim/rotate/delete old records to stay under a size budget" — owner directive 2026-10-11: the ledger is sacred, a 100 GB session must open, and no existing record may be lost. Rotation is allowed ONLY as split-and-retain (all `.part-NN` siblings kept and reassembled by the reader); repair keeps its `.bak` until the user explicitly removes it. Retracted.

## Incident (2026-10-11, all numbers measured with `stat -f %z` and `LC_ALL=C grep -c '"type":"compaction"'`)

The owner tried to open two sessions from the fa TUI session picker; both failed with `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session <path>: … exceeds the 2.0 GiB full-open bound`:

| Session | Created | Bytes | Size | Compaction records |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01a0d73f` ("network") | 2026-09-25 | 2,737,991,964 | 2.54 GiB | **0** in 2.7 GB of JSONL |
| `e7a689` (.worktrees/issue/355/ssh/followup) | 2026-09-14 | 2,912,096,469 | 2.91 GB | 51 |
| `01a06644` ("goal_builder") | 2026-09-03 | 2,236,083,302 | 2.08 GiB | 6 |

Sessions live under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/<slug>/`. Measured growth: ~0.4–0.6 GB/week on active named sessions.

## Mechanism chain (pinned facts — each verified against the working tree 2026-10-11)

- **(a) Append-only forever.** Session JSONL grows monotonically; compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file; nothing rotates or trims by size.
- **(b) Growth drivers.** Measured on goal_builder's last 500 MB (10,196 records): hidden `model_request_summary` custom records ≈ **0.7 MB EACH** (one per outbound LLM request — they persist a request-detail snapshot for the trajectory Request tab), plus multi-MB toolResult records (full test-run logs). Top records in the chunk: one 1.5 MB toolResult, then an unbroken run of 0.7 MB model_request_summary records.
- **(c) The windowed tail-reader EXISTS and is the intended design.** `WindowedSessionStorage.open` via `SessionRepo.open(metadata, windowed: true)` at lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:343 (doc comment: "the app's chat path, issue #135 … only the header plus the newest chunk are materialized"). The CLI resume `_loadSession` opens windowed (lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:582) and pages back only to the newest compaction boundary under a token budget (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`, gh-968 parity budget).
- **(d) BUT seven legacy call sites still take the DEFAULT full open (windowed:false):**
  1. lib/src/cli/agent_cli_pickers.dart:74 — TUI session picker `_tuiPickSession` does `_repo.open(metadata)`; the catch at :82 prints exactly the observed `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session …`. **← the user's exact failure path.**
  2. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:611 — `_loadSession` full-open FALLBACK when `ensureCompactionBoundaryResident` returns false (a marathon with NO compaction boundary). The "network" session has 0 compaction records → even the main resume path degenerates to full open → guaranteed refusal past 2 GiB.
  3. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:196 — `_resumeLastSession` full open.
  4. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:492 — name-resolution fallback loop, full-open PER SESSION until name match.
  5. lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:64,67,71 — `fa trajectory view/tail/cost/inspect` resolve via `repo.open(metadata)` full.
  6. bin/fah_trajectory.dart:94 — headless trajectory full open.
  7. lib/src/cli/agent_commands.dart:314 — `_openChildSession` (subagent transcript preview) full open.
- **(e) The backstop itself.** `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` (lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30); refusal thrown at :641 and :752 with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` (gh-1073 — added because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile).

### Amplification

The backstop converted a silent heap explosion into a loud refusal — but nothing on the WRITE side slows growth, and nothing on the READ side migrates the legacy call sites to windowed. So every long-lived named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. The gh-1073 refusal message even prescribes `fa --session …` and `fa session repair` — both of which themselves degenerate to a refuse…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);

blocks.text:
# gh-1555: [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop; legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable

## Description

## Goal — unbounded session JSONL growth defeats the 2 GiB full-open backstop (v1, initial draft)

One sentence: **every session remains openable forever at ANY size — 100 GB included — through lazy, tail-first, bounded-memory reads, and no ledger record is ever lost**: size is a read-pattern problem, never a deletion problem.

Today a session JSONL is append-only forever: compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file, and nothing rotates or trims by size. The gh-1073 backstop (`defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30`, lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30) converted the old silent heap explosion into a loud `SessionException` refusal — but nothing on the write side slows growth and nothing on the read side migrates the legacy full-open call sites to the existing windowed reader. So every active named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. This happened in production on 2026-10-11 (incident below). This card changes both sides: all tail/preview/trajectory read paths migrate to windowed/token-budgeted opens, and the ledger gains a size-based rotation/trim plus write-side caps on the dominant growth drivers.

## Owner directive (2026-10-11, supersedes any size-budget thinking below)

- **Sessions are never lost.** Not by trim, not by rotation, not by repair, not by write-side cap applied retroactively. A 100 GB ledger is a valid ledger. Any solution whose size story involves deleting or truncating EXISTING records is rejected by definition.
- **Openability is unconditional.** Picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — all must work on a 100 GB session with bounded memory. If a path cannot be made lazy, the path is buggy, not the session "too big".
- **Context-meter continuity across close/reopen.** A session closed showing 59% context usage reopens showing the same 59% — the resume boundary (newest compaction boundary, or the token-budget tail for a boundary-less marathon) must reconstruct EXACTLY the context the live loop carried at exit, not an approximation. Wrong boundary = wrong meter = a regression the owner can see.
- **Lazy loading everywhere, export included.** Today `exportTrajectoryJson`/`exportTrajectoryMarkdown` (lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:16,33) take a fully materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` — pure functions over `snapshot.records`, no IO. That means export transitively requires the full open it should avoid. Export must become scan-and-emit streaming: read records in bounded chunks, serialize incrementally to the sink, never materialize the snapshot.
- **Forward-looking write-side reduction** (W3) is permitted ONLY as opt-in and only for FUTURE records, and even then is an owner-call open question — never the mechanism that makes old sessions openable.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted framing 1:** "just raise/disable the 2 GiB bound" — the bound exists because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile (gh-1073); raising it re-opens the OOM. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 2:** "compaction alone fixes size" — compaction APPENDS a summary record; it never shrinks the file. The "network" incident session reached 2.54 GiB with **zero** compaction records; the ssh/followup session reached 2.91 GB **with** 51 compaction records. Compaction reduces model context, not bytes on disk. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 3:** "this is a read-side-only fix" — migrating call sites keeps the bomb ticking at 0.4–0.6 GB/week; the write side needs caps and a trim story. Retracted as insufficient (kept as the core tier, not the whole card).
- **Retracted framing 4:** "trim/rotate/delete old records to stay under a size budget" — owner directive 2026-10-11: the ledger is sacred, a 100 GB session must open, and no existing record may be lost. Rotation is allowed ONLY as split-and-retain (all `.part-NN` siblings kept and reassembled by the reader); repair keeps its `.bak` until the user explicitly removes it. Retracted.

## Incident (2026-10-11, all numbers measured with `stat -f %z` and `LC_ALL=C grep -c '"type":"compaction"'`)

The owner tried to open two sessions from the fa TUI session picker; both failed with `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session <path>: … exceeds the 2.0 GiB full-open bound`:

| Session | Created | Bytes | Size | Compaction records |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01a0d73f` ("network") | 2026-09-25 | 2,737,991,964 | 2.54 GiB | **0** in 2.7 GB of JSONL |
| `e7a689` (.worktrees/issue/355/ssh/followup) | 2026-09-14 | 2,912,096,469 | 2.91 GB | 51 |
| `01a06644` ("goal_builder") | 2026-09-03 | 2,236,083,302 | 2.08 GiB | 6 |

Sessions live under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/<slug>/`. Measured growth: ~0.4–0.6 GB/week on active named sessions.

## Mechanism chain (pinned facts — each verified against the working tree 2026-10-11)

- **(a) Append-only forever.** Session JSONL grows monotonically; compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file; nothing rotates or trims by size.
- **(b) Growth drivers.** Measured on goal_builder's last 500 MB (10,196 records): hidden `model_request_summary` custom records ≈ **0.7 MB EACH** (one per outbound LLM request — they persist a request-detail snapshot for the trajectory Request tab), plus multi-MB toolResult records (full test-run logs). Top records in the chunk: one 1.5 MB toolResult, then an unbroken run of 0.7 MB model_request_summary records.

## Owner directive (2026-10-11, supersedes any size-budget thinking below)

- **Sessions are never lost.** Not by trim, not by rotation, not by repair, not by write-side cap applied retroactively. A 100 GB ledger is a valid ledger. Any solution whose size story involves deleting or truncating EXISTING records is rejected by definition.
- **Openability is unconditional.** Picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — all must work on a 100 GB session with bounded memory. If a path cannot be made lazy, the path is buggy, not the session "too big".
- **Context-meter continuity across close/reopen.** A session closed showing 59% context usage reopens showing the same 59% — the resume boundary (newest compaction boundary, or the token-budget tail for a boundary-less marathon) must reconstruct EXACTLY the context the live loop carried at exit, not an approximation. Wrong boundary = wrong meter = a regression the owner can see.
- **Lazy loading everywhere, export included.** Today `exportTrajectoryJson`/`exportTrajectoryMarkdown` (lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:16,33) take a fully materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` — pure functions over `snapshot.records`, no IO. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
