# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.
===
1919:  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
2005:  `store_artefacts/metadata/{en,ru}/changelog.md`. Upload: `fastlane ios

blocks.text:
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.
===
1919:  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
2005:  `store_artefacts/metadata/{en,ru}/changelog.md`. Upload: `fastlane ios
The changelog is curated-only with an `## Unreleased` section. Adding a line there matches convention ("add new lines under `## Unreleased`"). I'll add a concise entry.

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1555 (W1, lazy/windowed-everywhere reads): the legacy full-open call
  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073
  2 GiB full-open backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path.
  The TUI session picker, `/resume`, and the boot name-resolution scan
  open windowed and resolve the display name through paged reads; the
  subagent transcript preview opens the child windowed (tail only); the
  `_loadSession` marathon fallback no longer degenerates to a refused
  full open when the boundary walk exhausts its page cap (it proceeds
  with the tail-anchored windowed session; the boot cap owns over-window
  residue); and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver opens windowed,
  paging the whole ledger in bounded doubling blocks via the new
  `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident` for the read-everything
  cost/inspect views. Trajectory export streaming (AC3a), split-and-retain
  rotation activation (W2), and the opt-in write-side caps (W3) remain
  follow-up work.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.
===
1919:  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
2005:  `store_artefacts/metadata/{en,ru}/changelog.md`. Upload: `fastlane ios

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.
===
1919:  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
2005:  `store_artefacts/metadata/{en,ru}/changelog.md`. Upload: `fastlane ios
The changelog is curated-only with an `## Unreleased` section. Adding a line there matches convention ("add new lines under `## Unreleased`"). I'll add a concise entry.

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1555 (W1, lazy/windowed-everywhere reads): the legacy full-open call
  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073
  2 GiB full-open backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path.
  The TUI session picker, `/resume`, and the boot name-resolution scan
  open windowed and resolve the display name through paged reads; the
  subagent transcript preview opens the child windowed (tail only); the
  `_loadSession` marathon fallback no longer degenerates to a refused
  full open when the boundary walk exhausts its page cap (it proceeds
  with the tail-anchored windowed session; the boot cap owns over-window
  residue); and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver opens windowed,
  paging the whole ledger in bounded doubling blocks via the new
  `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident` for the read-everything
  cost/inspect views. Trajectory export streaming (AC3a), split-and-retain
  rotation activation (W2), and the opt-in write-side caps (W3) remain
  follow-up work.

blocks.text:
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the

blocks.text:
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.
===
1919:  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
2005:  `store_artefacts/metadata/{en,ru}/changelog.md`. Upload: `fastlane ios
The changelog is curated-only with an `## Unreleased` section. Adding a line there matches convention ("add new lines under `## Unreleased`"). I'll add a concise entry.

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1555 (W1, lazy/windowed-everywhere reads): the legacy full-open call
  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073
  2 GiB full-open backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path.
  The TUI session picker, `/resume`, and the boot name-resolution scan
  open windowed and resolve the display name through paged reads; the
  subagent transcript preview opens the child windowed (tail only); the
  `_loadSession` marathon fallback no longer degenerates to a refused
  full open when the boundary walk exhausts its page cap (it proceeds
  with the tail-anchored windowed session; the boot cap owns over-window
  residue); and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver opens windowed,
  paging the whole ledger in bounded doubling blocks via the new
  `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident` for the read-everything
  cost/inspect views. Trajectory export streaming (AC3a), split-and-retain
  rotation activation (W2), and the opt-in write-side caps (W3) remain
  follow-up work.
","oldText":"## Unreleased
","path":"CHANGELOG.md"}

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.
===
1919:  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
2005:  `store_artefacts/metadata/{en,ru}/changelog.md`. Upload: `fastlane ios
The changelog is curated-only with an `## Unreleased` section. Adding a line there matches convention ("add new lines under `## Unreleased`"). I'll add a concise entry.

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1555 (W1, lazy/windowed-everywhere reads): the legacy full-open call
  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073
  2 GiB full-open backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path.
  The TUI session picker, `/resume`, and the boot name-resolution scan
  open windowed and resolve the display name through paged reads; the
  subagent transcript preview opens the child windowed (tail only); the
  `_loadSession` marathon fallback no longer degenerates to a refused
  full open when the boundary walk exhausts its page cap (it proceeds
  with the tail-anchored windowed session; the boot cap owns over-window
  residue); and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver opens windowed,
  paging the whole ledger in bounded doubling blocks via the new
  `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident` for the read-everything
  cost/inspect views. Trajectory export streaming (AC3a), split-and-retain
  rotation activation (W2), and the opt-in write-side caps (W3) remain
  follow-up work.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.

blocks.text:
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.
===
1919:  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
2005:  `store_artefacts/metadata/{en,ru}/changelog.md`. Upload: `fastlane ios
The changelog is curated-only with an `## Unreleased` section. Adding a line there matches convention ("add new lines under `## Unreleased`"). I'll add a concise entry.

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1555 (W1, lazy/windowed-everywhere reads): the legacy full-open call
  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073
  2 GiB full-open backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path.
  The TUI session picker, `/resume`, and the boot name-resolution scan
  open windowed and resolve the display name through paged reads; the
  subagent transcript preview opens the child windowed (tail only); the
  `_loadSession` marathon fallback no longer degenerates to a refused
  full open when the boundary walk exhausts its page cap (it proceeds
  with the tail-anchored windowed session; the boot cap owns over-window
  residue); and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver opens windowed,
  paging the whole ledger in bounded doubling blocks via the new
  `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident` for the read-everything
  cost/inspect views. Trajectory export streaming (AC3a), split-and-retain
  rotation activation (W2), and the opt-in write-side caps (W3) remain
  follow-up work.

blocks.text:
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.
===
1919:  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
2005:  `store_artefacts/metadata/{en,ru}/changelog.md`. Upload: `fastlane ios
The changelog is curated-only with an `## Unreleased` section. Adding a line there matches convention ("add new lines under `## Unreleased`"). I'll add a concise entry.

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1555 (W1, lazy/windowed-everywhere reads): the legacy full-open call
  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073
  2 GiB full-open backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path.
  The TUI session picker, `/resume`, and the boot name-resolution scan
  open windowed and resolve the display name through paged reads; the
  subagent transcript preview opens the child windowed (tail only); the
  `_loadSession` marathon fallback no longer degenerates to a refused
  full open when the boundary walk exhausts its page cap (it proceeds
  with the tail-anchored windowed session; the boot cap owns over-window
  residue); and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver opens windowed,
  paging the whole ledger in bounded doubling blocks via the new
  `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident` for the read-everything
  cost/inspect views. Trajectory export streaming (AC3a), split-and-retain
  rotation activation (W2), and the opt-in write-side caps (W3) remain
  follow-up work.

blocks.text:
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.
===
1919:  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
2005:  `store_artefacts/metadata/{en,ru}/changelog.md`. Upload: `fastlane ios
The changelog is curated-only with an `## Unreleased` section. Adding a line there matches convention ("add new lines under `## Unreleased`"). I'll add a concise entry.

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- gh-1555 (W1, lazy/windowed-everywhere reads): the legacy full-open call
  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073
  2 GiB full-open backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path.
  The TUI session picker, `/resume`, and the boot name-resolution scan
  open windowed and resolve the display name through paged reads; the
  subagent transcript preview opens the child windowed (tail only); the
  `_loadSession` marathon fallback no longer degenerates to a refused

  residue); and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver opens windowed,

  `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident` for the read-everything
  cost/inspect views. Trajectory export streaming (AC3a), split-and-retain
  rotation activation (W2), and the opt-in write-side caps (W3) remain

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1522: tag-sourced versions — the git tag is the single source of
  truth. The release-bot file bumps are retired: cutting a release = a
  tag + GitHub Release (zero commits to main, zero file mutations).
  Both pubspecs carry the fixed `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (CI guards
  hand-bumps), the publish job stamps the staged pubspec + generated
  changelog section from the tag (`scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`,
  staged version == tag guarded pre-upload), store builds stamp
  `--build-name/--build-number` from the derived tag version
  (`pubspec.lock` stops churning across releases), and
  `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from `git describe`.

- feat(usage): gh-1460 — the `fa-tokens:` segment-close line carries the
  session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is
  attributable to a model and therefore priceable. The fold now captures
  each segment's LAST-SEEN model id (the model that served the final
  request, the same string settings/UI display — mid-session fallback
  take-overs attribute the segment to the model that actually finished it;
  zero-filled fallbacks never clobber a seen model) and the pinned line
  shape grows an OPTIONAL `"model":"<id>"` key after `"segment"` — omitted
  when no model was observed, so legacy lines parse unchanged and the
  pinned regex (`usageTokensLogPattern`, gh-1241 AC7) keeps matching both
  shapes. usage.json's schema is untouched (the model is rebuildable from
  the chain, I6); old consumers using tolerant JSON ignore the new key,
  and the repo's single strict consumer (the pinned constant) is updated
  in the same change.
===
1919:  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
2005:  `store_artefacts/metadata/{en,ru}/changelog.md`. Upload: `fastlane ios

- gh-1555 (W1, lazy/windowed-everywhere reads): the legacy full-open call
  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073

  The TUI session picker, `/resume`, and the boot name-resolution scan

  `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident` for the read-everything
  cost/inspect views. Trajectory export streaming (AC3a), split-and-retain
  rotation activation (W2), and the opt-in write-side caps (W3) remain

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm

    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.

    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the

  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
