    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf

    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need

    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded

    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:

  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with

    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the

  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only

    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

Where's the cost? Candidates:
1. `getPathToRoot(leaf)` per page → but pages = ~9.
2. `_indexChunk(chunk, prepend: true)` — 9 calls.
3. `readBlockBefore` per page: reads + `_parseAllLines` — total work ≈ full parse (823ms-ish).
4. Something quadratic across pages.

Suspect #4: with eviction SUSPENDED, the window grows to 30k records. But what does `_readOlderBlock` do besides reading? `_indexChunk`. And in the growOlderUntil loop: `branch = await getPathToRoot(leaf)` per page — getPathToRoot walks from leaf via parentId through `_byId` — O(n) each, 9 pages — 270k ops, nothing.

Hmm — what about `shallowGiantCustoms: true`? Not relevant here (no giant customs).

What about `_splitLines` — per page strip scan, total = file size, fine.

`_parseAllLines` — parses each strip's lines. Total = all lines once. Fine.

So what's slow?? Let me profile: add timers inside? Quicker: test hypotheses by timing `readBlockBefore` total vs the rest. Or check `_indexChunk` for something O(window): if `_indexChunk` prepends entries into `_entries` list via insert(0, ...) per record — O(n) per record → O(n²) total!! tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

blocks.text:
The walk itself is 3291ms. The full open does the equivalent read+parse in ~800ms. So per-page work has ~2.5s of extra. What differs per page?

Full open streamed scan (`_openStreamedLocked`): SessionLineScanner over ranges, parse via `_parseExecutor`? No — check how full open parses: maybe it uses the parseExecutor pool when available... none here. Let me look at what readBlockBefore does vs the streamed scan:

1. `_readStripLines(limit, maxBytes)`: span starts at maxBytes. What is defaultChunkBytes? Let me check — maybe 256KB. span doubles until a complete line fits. Each iteration reads [limit-span, limit). Normally 1 iteration.
2. `_splitLines(bytes, lo)` — scan for \n.
3. `_parseAllLines(lines)` — parse each line.

Hypothesis: `_parseAllLines` runs on the `parseExecutor`... if null, inline. Same as scanner.

What about JSON decode: line bytes → utf8 decode → jsonDecode → SessionRecord.fromJson? The streamed scan may use a FASTER shallow/deferred parse? Actually! I remember session_storage streamed open has "shallow-parse header extraction"... no.

Alternatively the walk's `getPathToRoot(leaf)` + `_keptPathResident` per page... O(N) small.

Hmm — what about `_readOlderBlock`'s `chunk.entries.length` — with maxRecords: 200 → blockRecords starts at _chunkRecords = 200 records?? WAIT. Look at growOlderUntil: `var blockRecords = _chunkRecords; var blockBytes = _chunkBytes;` then per page `blockRecords *= 2` capped at maxWalkBlockRecords=4096, blockBytes capped at 64MB. But `readBlockBefore(top, maxRecords: blockRecords, maxBytes: blockBytes)` — the strip is capped by BOTH: entries.length > maxRecords → sublist keeps the NEWEST maxRecords of the strip and sets hasOlder=true... 

CRITICAL BUG (perf): if maxRecords caps the block (e.g., blockRecords=200 for page 1), the entries BELOW the kept 200 (older ones in the same strip) are DISCARDED but `_windowTopOffset = chunk.firstOffset` advances only to the first KEPT entry's offset — the older discarded part of the strip is re-read on the next page! With records ~1KB each: 200 records ≈ 200KB per page. 32.5MB / 200KB = 160 pages! Each page re-reads + re-parses the strip up to 2× its size (the discarded partial). Doubling: pages: 200,400,800,1600,3200,4096,4096... capped at 4096 records/page ≈ 4MB. So ~12-15 pages, each reading a strip of size blockBytes (capped by maxBytes too — defaultChunkBytes?).

What's defaultChunkBytes? If defaultChunkBytes = 512KB then blockBytes doubles 512K→1M→2M→4M→8M→16M→32M→64M: total read ≈ 127MB for a 32.5MB file → 4× read amplification, PLUS each strip's parse. And each page also re-reads/re-parses the discarded older segment? No — next page anchors at the kept-first's offset, so each byte is read... wait: strip [top-span, top). Keep newest 200 records → firstOffset = offset of the 200th-newest record in the strip. Next page reads [firstOffset - span', firstOffset). So no re-read; the discarded older portion of the strip is NEVER read again (the next strip covers it). Hmm, so each byte read once. Total ≈ 32.5MB.

BUT: the per-record cap at 200/400/.../4096 means per-page `_parseAllLines` parses the WHOLE strip (span bytes, up to 64MB... no wait — strip is maxBytes=blockBytes AND records capped after parse. Parse cost = strip size. Total parse ≈ file size. Read total: strips double: 512K+1M+2M+...+32M = 64MB-ish. So ~2× read+parse amplification ≈ 1.6-1.7s? Close to the observed 3.3s maybe with JIT variance. And the full open reads exactly 32.5MB once.

So the fix for the walk: start with BIGGER initial blocks. growOlderUntil starts at `_chunkRecords/_chunkBytes` (the interactive chunk size — small, for UI paging) and doubles per page. For a whole-ledger walk that's read-amplifying: sum of doubling geometric series ≈ 2× file. Plus per-page strip re-split.

Options:
a) In `ensureWholeLedgerResident`, call growOlderUntil with larger starting block? The start sizes are internal (`_chunkRecords`, `_chunkBytes` fields). Add optional `initialBlockRecords`/`initialBlockBytes` params to growOlderUntil, and have ensureWholeLedgerResident pass maxWalkBlockRecords/maxWalkBlockBytes directly (a single 64MB strip per page, no doubling ramp). Pages: ceil(32.5MB/64MB)=1 page + tail... blockRecords cap 4096: 30k records need 8 pages of 4096. Each page reads ≤64MB strip... strips: 32MB last... total read ≈ 32.5MB × ~1.0-1.5.

Actually with blockBytes=64MB and blockRecords=4096 from the start: page strips: readBlockBefore reads strip of 64MB → capped at 4096 records (sublist keeps newest 4096 → ~4MB) — WASTEFUL: it reads a 64MB strip to keep 4MB! The maxRecords cap makes big strips useless. Better: size the strip to the RECORD cap: bytes-per-record average... The reader doesn't know record sizes ahead.

Hmm — actually rethink: for whole-ledger walk, the natural primitive is the STREAMED SCAN (like the full open's SessionLineScanner): read sequentially from the file head in bounded chunks, parse incrementally, append to index. That's exactly what `_openStreamedLocked` does. But records arrive oldest-first while the windowed index needs... appending oldest-first at the HEAD — order doesn't matter for maps, but `_entries` must stay file-ordered — prepending oldest-first = repeated insertAll(0, chunk) per page → O(total²/page_size)... with insertAll(0, list) each page costs O(window) memmove — total O(N²/page) — no good for big N with many pages. Could collect pages and build the final list once — but intermediate pages... We could accumulate parsed pages in a list-of-pages and only splice into _entries ONCE at the end. But _entries feeds getPathToRoot during the walk (the loop needs branch each iteration for found/budget checks — but with found=(_)=>false and tokenBudget=null, the per-page branch check is `branch.any(found) && ...` → false always; and `if (!_hasOlder) return true`. And `_keptPathResident`? Only checked when found matches. So for ensureWholeLedgerResident the per-page branch recompute is useless work — but growOlderUntil is shared.

Pragmatic approach: keep growOlderUntil but make the block sizing smarter for deep walks:
- The real cost issue: doubling from small start reads ~2× and parses ~2×, plus per-page strip overhead. 2× of 819ms ≈ 1.6s, observed 3.3s. There's more: per page, `readBlockBefore` ALSO stats the file (`await stat()`), `_readStripLines` may double spans for line alignment (each page: the strip's first line is partial → discarded — with 4MB strips, tiny waste).

Where's the remaining 2×? Let me count pages concretely: defaultChunkBytes — need the value.

blocks.text:
The walk itself is 3291ms. The full open does the equivalent read+parse in ~800ms. So per-page work has ~2.5s of extra. What differs per page?

Full open streamed scan (`_openStreamedLocked`): SessionLineScanner over ranges, parse via `_parseExecutor`? No — check how full open parses: maybe it uses the parseExecutor pool when available... none here. Let me look at what readBlockBefore does vs the streamed scan:

1. `_readStripLines(limit, maxBytes)`: span starts at maxBytes. What is defaultChunkBytes? Let me check — maybe 256KB. span doubles until a complete line fits. Each iteration reads [limit-span, limit). Normally 1 iteration.
2. `_splitLines(bytes, lo)` — scan for \n.
3. `_parseAllLines(lines)` — parse each line.

Hypothesis: `_parseAllLines` runs on the `parseExecutor`... if null, inline. Same as scanner.

What about JSON decode: line bytes → utf8 decode → jsonDecode → SessionRecord.fromJson? The streamed scan may use a FASTER shallow/deferred parse? Actually! I remember session_storage streamed open has "shallow-parse header extraction"... no.

Alternatively the walk's `getPathToRoot(leaf)` + `_keptPathResident` per page... O(N) small.

Hmm — what about `_readOlderBlock`'s `chunk.entries.length` — with maxRecords: 200 → blockRecords starts at _chunkRecords = 200 records?? WAIT. Look at growOlderUntil: `var blockRecords = _chunkRecords; var blockBytes = _chunkBytes;` then per page `blockRecords *= 2` capped at maxWalkBlockRecords=4096, blockBytes capped at 64MB. But `readBlockBefore(top, maxRecords: blockRecords, maxBytes: blockBytes)` — the strip is capped by BOTH: entries.length > maxRecords → sublist keeps the NEWEST maxRecords of the strip and sets hasOlder=true... 

CRITICAL BUG (perf): if maxRecords caps the block (e.g., blockRecords=200 for page 1), the entries BELOW the kept 200 (older ones in the same strip) are DISCARDED but `_windowTopOffset = chunk.firstOffset` advances only to the first KEPT entry's offset — the older discarded part of the strip is re-read on the next page! With records ~1KB each: 200 records ≈ 200KB per page. 32.5MB / 200KB = 160 pages! Each page re-reads + re-parses the strip up to 2× its size (the discarded partial). Doubling: pages: 200,400,800,1600,3200,4096,4096... capped at 4096 records/page ≈ 4MB. So ~12-15 pages, each reading a strip of size blockBytes (capped by maxBytes too — defaultChunkBytes?).

What's defaultChunkBytes? If defaultChunkBytes = 512KB then blockBytes doubles 512K→1M→2M→4M→8M→16M→32M→64M: total read ≈ 127MB for a 32.5MB file → 4× read amplification, PLUS each strip's parse. And each page also re-reads/re-parses the discarded older segment? No — next page anchors at the kept-first's offset, so each byte is read... wait: strip [top-span, top). Keep newest 200 records → firstOffset = offset of the 200th-newest record in the strip. Next page reads [firstOffset - span', firstOffset). So no re-read; the discarded older portion of the strip is NEVER read again (the next strip covers it). Hmm, so each byte read once. Total ≈ 32.5MB.

BUT: the per-record cap at 200/400/.../4096 means per-page `_parseAllLines` parses the WHOLE strip (span bytes, up to 64MB... no wait — strip is maxBytes=blockBytes AND records capped after parse. Parse cost = strip size. Total parse ≈ file size. Read total: strips double: 512K+1M+2M+...+32M = 64MB-ish. So ~2× read+parse amplification ≈ 1.6-1.7s? Close to the observed 3.3s maybe with JIT variance. And the full open reads exactly 32.5MB once.

So the fix for the walk: start with BIGGER initial blocks. growOlderUntil starts at `_chunkRecords/_chunkBytes` (the interactive chunk size — small, for UI paging) and doubles per page. For a whole-ledger walk that's read-amplifying: sum of doubling geometric series ≈ 2× file. Plus per-page strip re-split.

Options:
a) In `ensureWholeLedgerResident`, call growOlderUntil with larger starting block? The start sizes are internal (`_chunkRecords`, `_chunkBytes` fields). Add optional `initialBlockRecords`/`initialBlockBytes` params to growOlderUntil, and have ensureWholeLedgerResident pass maxWalkBlockRecords/maxWalkBlockBytes directly (a single 64MB strip per page, no doubling ramp). Pages: ceil(32.5MB/64MB)=1 page + tail... blockRecords cap 4096: 30k records need 8 pages of 4096. Each page reads ≤64MB strip... strips: 32MB last... total read ≈ 32.5MB × ~1.0-1.5.

Actually with blockBytes=64MB and blockRecords=4096 from the start: page strips: readBlockBefore reads strip of 64MB → capped at 4096 records (sublist keeps newest 4096 → ~4MB) — WASTEFUL: it reads a 64MB strip to keep 4MB! The maxRecords cap makes big strips useless. Better: size the strip to the RECORD cap: bytes-per-record average... The reader doesn't know record sizes ahead.

Hmm — actually rethink: for whole-ledger walk, the natural primitive is the STREAMED SCAN (like the full open's SessionLineScanner): read sequentially from the file head in bounded chunks, parse incrementally, append to index. That's exactly what `_openStreamedLocked` does. But records arrive oldest-first while the windowed index needs... appending oldest-first at the HEAD — order doesn't matter for maps, but `_entries` must stay file-ordered — prepending oldest-first = repeated insertAll(0, chunk) per page → O(total²/page_size)... with insertAll(0, list) each page costs O(window) memmove — total O(N²/page) — no good for big N with many pages. Could collect pages and build the final list once — but intermediate pages... We could accumulate parsed pages in a list-of-pages and only splice into _entries ONCE at the end. But _entries feeds getPathToRoot during the walk (the loop needs branch each iteration for found/budget checks — but with found=(_)=>false and tokenBudget=null, the per-page branch check is `branch.any(found) && ...` → false always; and `if (!_hasOlder) return true`. And `_keptPathResident`? Only checked when found matches. So for ensureWholeLedgerResident the per-page branch recompute is useless work — but growOlderUntil is shared.

Pragmatic approach: keep growOlderUntil but make the block sizing smarter for deep walks:
- The real cost issue: doubling from small start reads ~2× and parses ~2×, plus per-page strip overhead. 2× of 819ms ≈ 1.6s, observed 3.3s. There's more: per page, `readBlockBefore` ALSO stats the file (`await stat()`), `_readStripLines` may double spans for line alignment (each page: the strip's first line is partial → discarded — with 4MB strips, tiny waste).

Look at growOlderUntil: `var blockRecords = _chunkRecords; var blockBytes = _chunkBytes;` then per page `blockRecords *= 2` capped at maxWalkBlockRecords=4096, blockBytes capped at 64MB. But `readBlockBefore(top, maxRecords: blockRecords, maxBytes: blockBytes)` — the strip is capped by BOTH: entries.length > maxRecords → sublist keeps the NEWEST maxRecords of the strip and sets hasOlder=true... 

CRITICAL BUG (perf): if maxRecords caps the block (e.g., blockRecords=200 for page 1), the entries BELOW the kept 200 (older ones in the same strip) are DISCARDED but `_windowTopOffset = chunk.firstOffset` advances only to the first KEPT entry's offset — the older discarded part of the strip is re-read on the next page! With records ~1KB each: 200 records ≈ 200KB per page. 32.5MB / 200KB = 160 pages! Each page re-reads + re-parses the strip up to 2× its size (the discarded partial). Doubling: pages: 200,400,800,1600,3200,4096,4096... capped at 4096 records/page ≈ 4MB. So ~12-15 pages, each reading a strip of size blockBytes (capped by maxBytes too — defaultChunkBytes?).

What's defaultChunkBytes? If defaultChunkBytes = 512KB then blockBytes doubles 512K→1M→2M→4M→8M→16M→32M→64M: total read ≈ 127MB for a 32.5MB file → 4× read amplification, PLUS each strip's parse. And each page also re-reads/re-parses the discarded older segment? No — next page anchors at the kept-first's offset, so each byte is read... wait: strip [top-span, top). Keep newest 200 records → firstOffset = offset of the 200th-newest record in the strip. Next page reads [firstOffset - span', firstOffset). So no re-read; the discarded older portion of the strip is NEVER read again (the next strip covers it). Hmm, so each byte read once. Total ≈ 32.5MB.

BUT: the per-record cap at 200/400/.../4096 means per-page `_parseAllLines` parses the WHOLE strip (span bytes, up to 64MB... no wait — strip is maxBytes=blockBytes AND records capped after parse. Parse cost = strip size. Total parse ≈ file size. Read total: strips double: 512K+1M+2M+...+32M = 64MB-ish. So ~2× read+parse amplification ≈ 1.6-1.7s? Close to the observed 3.3s maybe with JIT variance. And the full open reads exactly 32.5MB once.

So the fix for the walk: start with BIGGER initial blocks. growOlderUntil starts at `_chunkRecords/_chunkBytes` (the interactive chunk size — small, for UI paging) and doubles per page. For a whole-ledger walk that's read-amplifying: sum of doubling geometric series ≈ 2× file. Plus per-page strip re-split.

a) In `ensureWholeLedgerResident`, call growOlderUntil with larger starting block? The start sizes are internal (`_chunkRecords`, `_chunkBytes` fields). Add optional `initialBlockRecords`/`initialBlockBytes` params to growOlderUntil, and have ensureWholeLedgerResident pass maxWalkBlockRecords/maxWalkBlockBytes directly (a single 64MB strip per page, no doubling ramp). Pages: ceil(32.5MB/64MB)=1 page + tail... blockRecords cap 4096: 30k records need 8 pages of 4096. Each page reads ≤64MB strip... strips: 32MB last... total read ≈ 32.5MB × ~1.0-1.5.

Actually with blockBytes=64MB and blockRecords=4096 from the start: page strips: readBlockBefore reads strip of 64MB → capped at 4096 records (sublist keeps newest 4096 → ~4MB) — WASTEFUL: it reads a 64MB strip to keep 4MB! The maxRecords cap makes big strips useless. Better: size the strip to the RECORD cap: bytes-per-record average... The reader doesn't know record sizes ahead.

Hmm — actually rethink: for whole-ledger walk, the natural primitive is the STREAMED SCAN (like the full open's SessionLineScanner): read sequentially from the file head in bounded chunks, parse incrementally, append to index. That's exactly what `_openStreamedLocked` does. But records arrive oldest-first while the windowed index needs... appending oldest-first at the HEAD — order doesn't matter for maps, but `_entries` must stay file-ordered — prepending oldest-first = repeated insertAll(0, chunk) per page → O(total²/page_size)... with insertAll(0, list) each page costs O(window) memmove — total O(N²/page) — no good for big N with many pages. 3. `_parseAllLines(lines)` — parse each line.

Hypothesis: `_parseAllLines` runs on the `parseExecutor`... if null, inline. Same as scanner.

What about JSON decode: line bytes → utf8 decode → jsonDecode → SessionRecord.fromJson? The streamed scan may use a FASTER shallow/deferred parse? Actually! I remember session_storage streamed open has "shallow-parse header extraction"... no.

Alternatively the walk's `getPathToRoot(leaf)` + `_keptPathResident` per page... O(N) small.

Hmm — what about `_readOlderBlock`'s `chunk.entries.length` — with maxRecords: 200 → blockRecords starts at _chunkRecords = 200 records?? WAIT. Look at growOlderUntil: `var blockRecords = _chunkRecords; var blockBytes = _chunkBytes;` then per page `blockRecords *= 2` capped at maxWalkBlockRecords=4096, blockBytes capped at 64MB. But `readBlockBefore(top, maxRecords: blockRecords, maxBytes: blockBytes)` — the strip is capped by BOTH: entries.length > maxRecords → sublist keeps the NEWEST maxRecords of the strip and sets hasOlder=true... 

CRITICAL BUG (perf): if maxRecords caps the block (e.g., blockRecords=200 for page 1), the entries BELOW the kept 200 (older ones in the same strip) are DISCARDED but `_windowTopOffset = chunk.firstOffset` advances only to the first KEPT entry's offset — the older discarded part of the strip is re-read on the next page! With records ~1KB each: 200 records ≈ 200KB per page. 32.5MB / 200KB = 160 pages! Each page re-reads + re-parses the strip up to 2× its size (the discarded partial). Doubling: pages: 200,400,800,1600,3200,4096,4096... capped at 4096 records/page ≈ 4MB. So ~12-15 pages, each reading a strip of size blockBytes (capped by maxBytes too — defaultChunkBytes?).

What's defaultChunkBytes? If defaultChunkBytes = 512KB then blockBytes doubles 512K→1M→2M→4M→8M→16M→32M→64M: total read ≈ 127MB for a 32.5MB file → 4× read amplification, PLUS each strip's parse. And each page also re-reads/re-parses the discarded older segment? No — next page anchors at the kept-first's offset, so each byte is read... wait: strip [top-span, top). Keep newest 200 records → firstOffset = offset of the 200th-newest record in the strip. Next page reads [firstOffset - span', firstOffset). So no re-read; the discarded older portion of the strip is NEVER read again (the next strip covers it). Hmm, so each byte read once. Total ≈ 32.5MB.

BUT: the per-record cap at 200/400/.../4096 means per-page `_parseAllLines` parses the WHOLE strip (span bytes, up to 64MB... no wait — strip is maxBytes=blockBytes AND records capped after parse. Parse cost = strip size. Total parse ≈ file size. Read total: strips double: 512K+1M+2M+...+32M = 64MB-ish. So ~2× read+parse amplification ≈ 1.6-1.7s? Close to the observed 3.3s maybe with JIT variance. And the full open reads exactly 32.5MB once.

So the fix for the walk: start with BIGGER initial blocks. growOlderUntil starts at `_chunkRecords/_chunkBytes` (the interactive chunk size — small, for UI paging) and doubles per page. For a whole-ledger walk that's read-amplifying: sum of doubling geometric series ≈ 2× file. Plus per-page strip re-split.

Options:
a) In `ensureWholeLedgerResident`, call growOlderUntil with larger starting block? The start sizes are internal (`_chunkRecords`, `_chunkBytes` fields). Add optional `initialBlockRecords`/`initialBlockBytes` params to growOlderUntil, and have ensureWholeLedgerResident pass maxWalkBlockRecords/maxWalkBlockBytes directly (a single 64MB strip per page, no doubling ramp). Pages: ceil(32.5MB/64MB)=1 page + tail... blockRecords cap 4096: 30k records need 8 pages of 4096. Each page reads ≤64MB strip... strips: 32MB last... total read ≈ 32.5MB × ~1.0-1.5.

Actually with blockBytes=64MB and blockRecords=4096 from the start: page strips: readBlockBefore reads strip of 64MB → capped at 4096 records (sublist keeps newest 4096 → ~4MB) — WASTEFUL: it reads a 64MB strip to keep 4MB! The maxRecords cap makes big strips useless. Better: size the strip to the RECORD cap: bytes-per-record average... The reader doesn't know record sizes ahead.

Hmm — actually rethink: for whole-ledger walk, the natural primitive is the STREAMED SCAN (like the full open's SessionLineScanner): read sequentially from the file head in bounded chunks, parse incrementally, append to index. That's exactly what `_openStreamedLocked` does. But records arrive oldest-first while the windowed index needs... appending oldest-first at the HEAD — order doesn't matter for maps, but `_entries` must stay file-ordered — prepending oldest-first = repeated insertAll(0, chunk) per page → O(total²/page_size)... with insertAll(0, list) each page costs O(window) memmove — total O(N²/page) — no good for big N with many pages. Could collect pages and build the final list once — but intermediate pages... We could accumulate parsed pages in a list-of-pages and only splice into _entries ONCE at the end. But _entries feeds getPathToRoot during the walk (the loop needs branch each iteration for found/budget checks — but with found=(_)=>false and tokenBudget=null, the per-page branch check is `branch.any(found) && ...` → false always; and `if (!_hasOlder) return true`. And `_keptPathResident`? Only checked when found matches. So for ensureWholeLedgerResident the per-page branch recompute is useless work — but growOlderUntil is shared.

Pragmatic approach: keep growOlderUntil but make the block sizing smarter for deep walks:
- The real cost issue: doubling from small start reads ~2× and parses ~2×, plus per-page strip overhead. 2× of 819ms ≈ 1.6s, observed 3.3s. 2. `_splitLines(bytes, lo)` — scan for \n.
3. `_parseAllLines(lines)` — parse each line.

Hypothesis: `_parseAllLines` runs on the `parseExecutor`... if null, inline. Same as scanner.

What about JSON decode: line bytes → utf8 decode → jsonDecode → SessionRecord.fromJson? The streamed scan may use a FASTER shallow/deferred parse? Actually! I remember session_storage streamed open has "shallow-parse header extraction"... no.

Alternatively the walk's `getPathToRoot(leaf)` + `_keptPathResident` per page... O(N) small.

Hmm — what about `_readOlderBlock`'s `chunk.entries.length` — with maxRecords: 200 → blockRecords starts at _chunkRecords = 200 records?? WAIT. Look at growOlderUntil: `var blockRecords = _chunkRecords; var blockBytes = _chunkBytes;` then per page `blockRecords *= 2` capped at maxWalkBlockRecords=4096, blockBytes capped at 64MB. But `readBlockBefore(top, maxRecords: blockRecords, maxBytes: blockBytes)` — the strip is capped by BOTH: entries.length > maxRecords → sublist keeps the NEWEST maxRecords of the strip and sets hasOlder=true... 

CRITICAL BUG (perf): if maxRecords caps the block (e.g., blockRecords=200 for page 1), the entries BELOW the kept 200 (older ones in the same strip) are DISCARDED but `_windowTopOffset = chunk.firstOffset` advances only to the first KEPT entry's offset — the older discarded part of the strip is re-read on the next page! With records ~1KB each: 200 records ≈ 200KB per page. 32.5MB / 200KB = 160 pages! Each page re-reads + re-parses the strip up to 2× its size (the discarded partial). Doubling: pages: 200,400,800,1600,3200,4096,4096... capped at 4096 records/page ≈ 4MB. So ~12-15 pages, each reading a strip of size blockBytes (capped by maxBytes too — defaultChunkBytes?).

What's defaultChunkBytes? If defaultChunkBytes = 512KB then blockBytes doubles 512K→1M→2M→4M→8M→16M→32M→64M: total read ≈ 127MB for a 32.5MB file → 4× read amplification, PLUS each strip's parse. And each page also re-reads/re-parses the discarded older segment? No — next page anchors at the kept-first's offset, so each byte is read... wait: strip [top-span, top). Keep newest 200 records → firstOffset = offset of the 200th-newest record in the strip. Next page reads [firstOffset - span', firstOffset). So no re-read; the discarded older portion of the strip is NEVER read again (the next strip covers it). Hmm, so each byte read once. Total ≈ 32.5MB.

BUT: the per-record cap at 200/400/.../4096 means per-page `_parseAllLines` parses the WHOLE strip (span bytes, up to 64MB... no wait — strip is maxBytes=blockBytes AND records capped after parse. Parse cost = strip size. Total parse ≈ file size. Read total: strips double: 512K+1M+2M+...+32M = 64MB-ish. So ~2× read+parse amplification ≈ 1.6-1.7s? Close to the observed 3.3s maybe with JIT variance. And the full open reads exactly 32.5MB once.

So the fix for the walk: start with BIGGER initial blocks. growOlderUntil starts at `_chunkRecords/_chunkBytes` (the interactive chunk size — small, for UI paging) and doubles per page. For a whole-ledger walk that's read-amplifying: sum of doubling geometric series ≈ 2× file. Plus per-page strip re-split.

Options:
a) In `ensureWholeLedgerResident`, call growOlderUntil with larger starting block? The start sizes are internal (`_chunkRecords`, `_chunkBytes` fields). Add optional `initialBlockRecords`/`initialBlockBytes` params to growOlderUntil, and have ensureWholeLedgerResident pass maxWalkBlockRecords/maxWalkBlockBytes directly (a single 64MB strip per page, no doubling ramp). Pages: ceil(32.5MB/64MB)=1 page + tail... blockRecords cap 4096: 30k records need 8 pages of 4096. Each page reads ≤64MB strip... strips: 32MB last... total read ≈ 32.5MB × ~1.0-1.5.

Actually with blockBytes=64MB and blockRecords=4096 from the start: page strips: readBlockBefore reads strip of 64MB → capped at 4096 records (sublist keeps newest 4096 → ~4MB) — WASTEFUL: it reads a 64MB strip to keep 4MB! The maxRecords cap makes big strips useless. Better: size the strip to the RECORD cap: bytes-per-record average... The reader doesn't know record sizes ahead.

Hmm — actually rethink: for whole-ledger walk, the natural primitive is the STREAMED SCAN (like the full open's SessionLineScanner): read sequentially from the file head in bounded chunks, parse incrementally, append to index. That's exactly what `_openStreamedLocked` does. But records arrive oldest-first while the windowed index needs... appending oldest-first at the HEAD — order doesn't matter for maps, but `_entries` must stay file-ordered — prepending oldest-first = repeated insertAll(0, chunk) per page → O(total²/page_size)... with insertAll(0, list) each page costs O(window) memmove — total O(N²/page) — no good for big N with many pages. Could collect pages and build the final list once — but intermediate pages... We could accumulate parsed pages in a list-of-pages and only splice into _entries ONCE at the end. But _entries feeds getPathToRoot during the walk (the loop needs branch each iteration for found/budget checks — but with found=(_)=>false and tokenBudget=null, the per-page branch check is `branch.any(found) && ...` → false always; and `if (!_hasOlder) return true`. And `_keptPathResident`? Only checked when found matches. So for ensureWholeLedgerResident the per-page branch recompute is useless work — but growOlderUntil is shared.

Pragmatic approach: keep growOlderUntil but make the block sizing smarter for deep walks:
- The real cost issue: doubling from small start reads ~2× and parses ~2×, plus per-page strip overhead. 2× of 819ms ≈ 1.6s, observed 3.3s. Hypothesis: `_parseAllLines` runs on the `parseExecutor`... if null, inline. Same as scanner.
