Alternatively the walk's `getPathToRoot(leaf)` + `_keptPathResident` per page... O(N) small.

Hmm — what about `_readOlderBlock`'s `chunk.entries.length` — with maxRecords: 200 → blockRecords starts at _chunkRecords = 200 records?? WAIT. Look at growOlderUntil: `var blockRecords = _chunkRecords; var blockBytes = _chunkBytes;` then per page `blockRecords *= 2` capped at maxWalkBlockRecords=4096, blockBytes capped at 64MB. But `readBlockBefore(top, maxRecords: blockRecords, maxBytes: blockBytes)` — the strip is capped by BOTH: entries.length > maxRecords → sublist keeps the NEWEST maxRecords of the strip and sets hasOlder=true... 

CRITICAL BUG (perf): if maxRecords caps the block (e.g., blockRecords=200 for page 1), the entries BELOW the kept 200 (older ones in the same strip) are DISCARDED but `_windowTopOffset = chunk.firstOffset` advances only to the first KEPT entry's offset — the older discarded part of the strip is re-read on the next page! With records ~1KB each: 200 records ≈ 200KB per page. 32.5MB / 200KB = 160 pages! Each page re-reads + re-parses the strip up to 2× its size (the discarded partial). Doubling: pages: 200,400,800,1600,3200,4096,4096... capped at 4096 records/page ≈ 4MB. So ~12-15 pages, each reading a strip of size blockBytes (capped by maxBytes too — defaultChunkBytes?).

What's defaultChunkBytes? If defaultChunkBytes = 512KB then blockBytes doubles 512K→1M→2M→4M→8M→16M→32M→64M: total read ≈ 127MB for a 32.5MB file → 4× read amplification, PLUS each strip's parse. And each page also re-reads/re-parses the discarded older segment? No — next page anchors at the kept-first's offset, so each byte is read... wait: strip [top-span, top). Keep newest 200 records → firstOffset = offset of the 200th-newest record in the strip. Next page reads [firstOffset - span', firstOffset). So no re-read; the discarded older portion of the strip is NEVER read again (the next strip covers it). Hmm, so each byte read once. Total ≈ 32.5MB.

BUT: the per-record cap at 200/400/.../4096 means per-page `_parseAllLines` parses the WHOLE strip (span bytes, up to 64MB... no wait — strip is maxBytes=blockBytes AND records capped after parse. Parse cost = strip size. Total parse ≈ file size. Read total: strips double: 512K+1M+2M+...+32M = 64MB-ish. So ~2× read+parse amplification ≈ 1.6-1.7s? Close to the observed 3.3s maybe with JIT variance. And the full open reads exactly 32.5MB once.

So the fix for the walk: start with BIGGER initial blocks. growOlderUntil starts at `_chunkRecords/_chunkBytes` (the interactive chunk size — small, for UI paging) and doubles per page. For a whole-ledger walk that's read-amplifying: sum of doubling geometric series ≈ 2× file. Plus per-page strip re-split.

Options:
a) In `ensureWholeLedgerResident`, call growOlderUntil with larger starting block? The start sizes are internal (`_chunkRecords`, `_chunkBytes` fields). Add optional `initialBlockRecords`/`initialBlockBytes` params to growOlderUntil, and have ensureWholeLedgerResident pass maxWalkBlockRecords/maxWalkBlockBytes directly (a single 64MB strip per page, no doubling ramp). Pages: ceil(32.5MB/64MB)=1 page + tail... blockRecords cap 4096: 30k records need 8 pages of 4096. Each page reads ≤64MB strip... strips: 32MB last... total read ≈ 32.5MB × ~1.0-1.5.

Actually with blockBytes=64MB and blockRecords=4096 from the start: page strips: readBlockBefore reads strip of 64MB → capped at 4096 records (sublist keeps newest 4096 → ~4MB) — WASTEFUL: it reads a 64MB strip to keep 4MB! The maxRecords cap makes big strips useless. Better: size the strip to the RECORD cap: bytes-per-record average... The reader doesn't know record sizes ahead.

Hmm — actually rethink: for whole-ledger walk, the natural primitive is the STREAMED SCAN (like the full open's SessionLineScanner): read sequentially from the file head in bounded chunks, parse incrementally, append to index. That's exactly what `_openStreamedLocked` does. But records arrive oldest-first while the windowed index needs... appending oldest-first at the HEAD — order doesn't matter for maps, but `_entries` must stay file-ordered — prepending oldest-first = repeated insertAll(0, chunk) per page → O(total²/page_size)... with insertAll(0, list) each page costs O(window) memmove — total O(N²/page) — no good for big N with many pages. Could collect pages and build the final list once — but intermediate pages... We could accumulate parsed pages in a list-of-pages and only splice into _entries ONCE at the end. But _entries feeds getPathToRoot during the walk (the loop needs branch each iteration for found/budget checks — but with found=(_)=>false and tokenBudget=null, the per-page branch check is `branch.any(found) && ...` → false always; and `if (!_hasOlder) return true`. And `_keptPathResident`? Only checked when found matches. So for ensureWholeLedgerResident the per-page branch recompute is useless work — but growOlderUntil is shared.

Pragmatic approach: keep growOlderUntil but make the block sizing smarter for deep walks:
- The real cost issue: doubling from small start reads ~2× and parses ~2×, plus per-page strip overhead. 2× of 819ms ≈ 1.6s, observed 3.3s. With records ~1KB each: 200 records ≈ 200KB per page. 32.5MB / 200KB = 160 pages! Each page re-reads + re-parses the strip up to 2× its size (the discarded partial). Doubling: pages: 200,400,800,1600,3200,4096,4096... capped at 4096 records/page ≈ 4MB. So ~12-15 pages, each reading a strip of size blockBytes (capped by maxBytes too — defaultChunkBytes?).

What's defaultChunkBytes? If defaultChunkBytes = 512KB then blockBytes doubles 512K→1M→2M→4M→8M→16M→32M→64M: total read ≈ 127MB for a 32.5MB file → 4× read amplification, PLUS each strip's parse. Keep newest 200 records → firstOffset = offset of the 200th-newest record in the strip. Next page reads [firstOffset - span', firstOffset). messages.preview: My slot math reversed the list (side-effect order ≠ list order). Fix:

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

The walk itself is 3291ms. The full open does the equivalent read+parse in ~800ms. So per-page work has ~2.5s of extra. What differs per page?

Full open streamed scan (`_openStreamedLocked`): SessionLineScanner over ranges, parse via `_parseExecutor`? No — check how full open parses: maybe it uses the parseExecutor pool when available... none here. Let me look at what readBlockBefore does vs the streamed scan:

1. `_readStripLines(limit, maxBytes)`: span starts at maxBytes. What is defaultChunkBytes? Let me check — maybe 256KB. span doubles until a complete line fits. Each iteration reads [limit-span, limit). Normally 1 iteration.
2. `_splitLines(bytes, lo)` — scan for \n.
3. `_parseAllLines(lines)` — parse each line.

Hypothesis: `_parseAllLines` runs on the `parseExecutor`... if null, inline. Same as scanner.

What about JSON decode: line bytes → utf8 decode → jsonDecode → SessionRecord.fromJson? The streamed scan may use a FASTER shallow/deferred parse? Actually! I remember session_storage streamed open has "shallow-parse header extraction"... no.

Alternatively the walk's `getPathToRoot(leaf)` + `_keptPathResident` per page... O(N) small.

Hmm — what about `_readOlderBlock`'s `chunk.entries.length` — with maxRecords: 200 → blockRecords starts at _chunkRecords = 200 records?? WAIT. Look at growOlderUntil: `var blockRecords = _chunkRecords; var blockBytes = _chunkBytes;` then per page `blockRecords *= 2` capped at maxWalkBlockRecords=4096, blockBytes capped at 64MB. But `readBlockBefore(top, maxRecords: blockRecords, maxBytes: blockBytes)` — the strip is capped by BOTH: entries.length > maxRecords → sublist keeps the NEWEST maxRecords of the strip and sets hasOlder=true... 

CRITICAL BUG (perf): if maxRecords caps the block (e.g., blockRecords=200 for page 1), the entries BELOW the kept 200 (older ones in the same strip) are DISCARDED but `_windowTopOffset = chunk.firstOffset` advances only to the first KEPT entry's offset — the older discarded part of the strip is re-read on the next page! With records ~1KB each: 200 records ≈ 200KB per page. 32.5MB / 200KB = 160 pages! Each page re-reads + re-parses the strip up to 2× its size (the discarded partial). Doubling: pages: 200,400,800,1600,3200,4096,4096... capped at 4096 records/page ≈ 4MB. So ~12-15 pages, each reading a strip of size blockBytes (capped by maxBytes too — defaultChunkBytes?).

What's defaultChunkBytes? If defaultChunkBytes = 512KB then blockBytes doubles 512K→1M→2M→4M→8M→16M→32M→64M: total read ≈ 127MB for a 32.5MB file → 4× read amplification, PLUS each strip's parse. And each page also re-reads/re-parses the discarded older segment? No — next page anchors at the kept-first's offset, so each byte is read... wait: strip [top-span, top). Keep newest 200 records → firstOffset = offset of the 200th-newest record in the strip. Next page reads [firstOffset - span', firstOffset). So no re-read; the discarded older portion of the strip is NEVER read again (the next strip covers it). Hmm, so each byte read once. Total ≈ 32.5MB.

BUT: the per-record cap at 200/400/.../4096 means per-page `_parseAllLines` parses the WHOLE strip (span bytes, up to 64MB... no wait — strip is maxBytes=blockBytes AND records capped after parse. Parse cost = strip size. Total parse ≈ file size. Read total: strips double: 512K+1M+2M+...+32M = 64MB-ish. So ~2× read+parse amplification ≈ 1.6-1.7s? Close to the observed 3.3s maybe with JIT variance. And the full open reads exactly 32.5MB once.

So the fix for the walk: start with BIGGER initial blocks. growOlderUntil starts at `_chunkRecords/_chunkBytes` (the interactive chunk size — small, for UI paging) and doubles per page. For a whole-ledger walk that's read-amplifying: sum of doubling geometric series ≈ 2× file. Plus per-page strip re-split.

Options:
a) In `ensureWholeLedgerResident`, call growOlderUntil with larger starting block? The start sizes are internal (`_chunkRecords`, `_chunkBytes` fields). Add optional `initialBlockRecords`/`initialBlockBytes` params to growOlderUntil, and have ensureWholeLedgerResident pass maxWalkBlockRecords/maxWalkBlockBytes directly (a single 64MB strip per page, no doubling ramp). Pages: ceil(32.5MB/64MB)=1 page + tail... blockRecords cap 4096: 30k records need 8 pages of 4096. Each page reads ≤64MB strip... strips: 32MB last... total read ≈ 32.5MB × ~1.0-1.5.

Actually with blockBytes=64MB and blockRecords=4096 from the start: page strips: readBlockBefore reads strip of 64MB → capped at 4096 records (sublist keeps newest 4096 → ~4MB) — WASTEFUL: it reads a 64MB strip to keep 4MB! The maxRecords cap makes big strips useless. Better: size the strip to the RECORD cap: bytes-per-record average... The reader doesn't know record sizes ahead.

Hmm — actually rethink: for whole-ledger walk, the natural primitive is the STREAMED SCAN (like the full open's SessionLineScanner): read sequentially from the file head in bounded chunks, parse incrementally, append to index. That's exactly what `_openStreamedLocked` does. But records arrive oldest-first while the windowed index needs... appending oldest-first at the HEAD — order doesn't matter for maps, but `_entries` must stay file-ordered — prepending oldest-first = repeated insertAll(0, chunk) per page → O(total²/page_size)... with insertAll(0, list) each page costs O(window) memmove — total O(N²/page) — no good for big N with many pages. Could collect pages and build the final list once — but intermediate pages... We could accumulate parsed pages in a list-of-pages and only splice into _entries ONCE at the end. But _entries feeds getPathToRoot during the walk (the loop needs branch each iteration for found/budget checks — but with found=(_)=>false and tokenBudget=null, the per-page branch check is `branch.any(found) && ...` → false always; and `if (!_hasOlder) return true`. And `_keptPathResident`? Only checked when found matches. So for ensureWholeLedgerResident the per-page branch recompute is useless work — but growOlderUntil is shared.

Pragmatic approach: keep growOlderUntil but make the block sizing smarter for deep walks:
- The real cost issue: doubling from small start reads ~2× and parses ~2×, plus per-page strip overhead. 2× of 819ms ≈ 1.6s, observed 3.3s. There's more: per page, `readBlockBefore` ALSO stats the file (`await stat()`), `_readStripLines` may double spans for line alignment (each page: the strip's first line is partial → discarded — with 4MB strips, tiny waste).

messages.preview: My slot math reversed the list (side-effect order ≠ list order). Fix:

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

messages.preview: My slot math reversed the list (side-effect order ≠ list order). Fix:

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

But `readBlockBefore(top, maxRecords: blockRecords, maxBytes: blockBytes)` — the strip is capped by BOTH: entries.length > maxRecords → sublist keeps the NEWEST maxRecords of the strip and sets hasOlder=true... 

CRITICAL BUG (perf): if maxRecords caps the block (e.g., blockRecords=200 for page 1), the entries BELOW the kept 200 (older ones in the same strip) are DISCARDED but `_windowTopOffset = chunk.firstOffset` advances only to the first KEPT entry's offset — the older discarded part of the strip is re-read on the next page! With records ~1KB each: 200 records ≈ 200KB per page. 32.5MB / 200KB = 160 pages! Each page re-reads + re-parses the strip up to 2× its size (the discarded partial). Doubling: pages: 200,400,800,1600,3200,4096,4096... capped at 4096 records/page ≈ 4MB. So ~12-15 pages, each reading a strip of size blockBytes (capped by maxBytes too — defaultChunkBytes?).

What's defaultChunkBytes? If defaultChunkBytes = 512KB then blockBytes doubles 512K→1M→2M→4M→8M→16M→32M→64M: total read ≈ 127MB for a 32.5MB file → 4× read amplification, PLUS each strip's parse. And each page also re-reads/re-parses the discarded older segment? No — next page anchors at the kept-first's offset, so each byte is read... wait: strip [top-span, top). Keep newest 200 records → firstOffset = offset of the 200th-newest record in the strip. Next page reads [firstOffset - span', firstOffset). So no re-read; the discarded older portion of the strip is NEVER read again (the next strip covers it). Hmm, so each byte read once. Total ≈ 32.5MB.

BUT: the per-record cap at 200/400/.../4096 means per-page `_parseAllLines` parses the WHOLE strip (span bytes, up to 64MB... no wait — strip is maxBytes=blockBytes AND records capped after parse. Parse cost = strip size. Total parse ≈ file size. Read total: strips double: 512K+1M+2M+...+32M = 64MB-ish. So ~2× read+parse amplification ≈ 1.6-1.7s? So the fix for the walk: start with BIGGER initial blocks. growOlderUntil starts at `_chunkRecords/_chunkBytes` (the interactive chunk size — small, for UI paging) and doubles per page. For a whole-ledger walk that's read-amplifying: sum of doubling geometric series ≈ 2× file. Plus per-page strip re-split.

The maxRecords cap makes big strips useless. Better: size the strip to the RECORD cap: bytes-per-record average... The reader doesn't know record sizes ahead.

Hmm — actually rethink: for whole-ledger walk, the natural primitive is the STREAMED SCAN (like the full open's SessionLineScanner): read sequentially from the file head in bounded chunks, parse incrementally, append to index. That's exactly what `_openStreamedLocked` does. But records arrive oldest-first while the windowed index needs... appending oldest-first at the HEAD — order doesn't matter for maps, but `_entries` must stay file-ordered — prepending oldest-first = repeated insertAll(0, chunk) per page → O(total²/page_size)... with insertAll(0, list) each page costs O(window) memmove — total O(N²/page) — no good for big N with many pages. Could collect pages and build the final list once — but intermediate pages... We could accumulate parsed pages in a list-of-pages and only splice into _entries ONCE at the end. messages.preview: My slot math reversed the list (side-effect order ≠ list order). Fix:

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

But `readBlockBefore(top, maxRecords: blockRecords, maxBytes: blockBytes)` — the strip is capped by BOTH: entries.length > maxRecords → sublist keeps the NEWEST maxRecords of the strip and sets hasOlder=true... 

CRITICAL BUG (perf): if maxRecords caps the block (e.g., blockRecords=200 for page 1), the entries BELOW the kept 200 (older ones in the same strip) are DISCARDED but `_windowTopOffset = chunk.firstOffset` advances only to the first KEPT entry's offset — the older discarded part of the strip is re-read on the next page! With records ~1KB each: 200 records ≈ 200KB per page. 32.5MB / 200KB = 160 pages! Each page re-reads + re-parses the strip up to 2× its size (the discarded partial). Doubling: pages: 200,400,800,1600,3200,4096,4096... capped at 4096 records/page ≈ 4MB. So ~12-15 pages, each reading a strip of size blockBytes (capped by maxBytes too — defaultChunkBytes?).

What's defaultChunkBytes? If defaultChunkBytes = 512KB then blockBytes doubles 512K→1M→2M→4M→8M→16M→32M→64M: total read ≈ 127MB for a 32.5MB file → 4× read amplification, PLUS each strip's parse. And each page also re-reads/re-parses the discarded older segment? No — next page anchors at the kept-first's offset, so each byte is read... wait: strip [top-span, top). Keep newest 200 records → firstOffset = offset of the 200th-newest record in the strip. Next page reads [firstOffset - span', firstOffset). So no re-read; the discarded older portion of the strip is NEVER read again (the next strip covers it). Hmm, so each byte read once. Total ≈ 32.5MB.

BUT: the per-record cap at 200/400/.../4096 means per-page `_parseAllLines` parses the WHOLE strip (span bytes, up to 64MB... no wait — strip is maxBytes=blockBytes AND records capped after parse. Parse cost = strip size. Total parse ≈ file size. Read total: strips double: 512K+1M+2M+...+32M = 64MB-ish. So ~2× read+parse amplification ≈ 1.6-1.7s? Close to the observed 3.3s maybe with JIT variance. And the full open reads exactly 32.5MB once.

So the fix for the walk: start with BIGGER initial blocks. growOlderUntil starts at `_chunkRecords/_chunkBytes` (the interactive chunk size — small, for UI paging) and doubles per page. For a whole-ledger walk that's read-amplifying: sum of doubling geometric series ≈ 2× file. Plus per-page strip re-split.

The maxRecords cap makes big strips useless. Better: size the strip to the RECORD cap: bytes-per-record average... The reader doesn't know record sizes ahead.

Hmm — actually rethink: for whole-ledger walk, the natural primitive is the STREAMED SCAN (like the full open's SessionLineScanner): read sequentially from the file head in bounded chunks, parse incrementally, append to index. That's exactly what `_openStreamedLocked` does. blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

messages.preview: My slot math reversed the list (side-effect order ≠ list order). Fix:

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The walk itself is 3291ms. The full open does the equivalent read+parse in ~800ms. So per-page work has ~2.5s of extra. What differs per page?

Full open streamed scan (`_openStreamedLocked`): SessionLineScanner over ranges, parse via `_parseExecutor`? No — check how full open parses: maybe it uses the parseExecutor pool when available... none here. Let me look at what readBlockBefore does vs the streamed scan:

1. `_readStripLines(limit, maxBytes)`: span starts at maxBytes. What is defaultChunkBytes? Let me check — maybe 256KB. span doubles until a complete line fits. Each iteration reads [limit-span, limit). Normally 1 iteration.
2. `_splitLines(bytes, lo)` — scan for \n.
3. `_parseAllLines(lines)` — parse each line.

Hypothesis: `_parseAllLines` runs on the `parseExecutor`... if null, inline. Same as scanner.

What about JSON decode: line bytes → utf8 decode → jsonDecode → SessionRecord.fromJson? The streamed scan may use a FASTER shallow/deferred parse? Actually! I remember session_storage streamed open has "shallow-parse header extraction"... no.

Alternatively the walk's `getPathToRoot(leaf)` + `_keptPathResident` per page... O(N) small.

Hmm — what about `_readOlderBlock`'s `chunk.entries.length` — with maxRecords: 200 → blockRecords starts at _chunkRecords = 200 records?? WAIT. Look at growOlderUntil: `var blockRecords = _chunkRecords; var blockBytes = _chunkBytes;` then per page `blockRecords *= 2` capped at maxWalkBlockRecords=4096, blockBytes capped at 64MB. But `readBlockBefore(top, maxRecords: blockRecords, maxBytes: blockBytes)` — the strip is capped by BOTH: entries.length > maxRecords → sublist keeps the NEWEST maxRecords of the strip and sets hasOlder=true... 

CRITICAL BUG (perf): if maxRecords caps the block (e.g., blockRecords=200 for page 1), the entries BELOW the kept 200 (older ones in the same strip) are DISCARDED but `_windowTopOffset = chunk.firstOffset` advances only to the first KEPT entry's offset — the older discarded part of the strip is re-read on the next page! With records ~1KB each: 200 records ≈ 200KB per page. 32.5MB / 200KB = 160 pages! Each page re-reads + re-parses the strip up to 2× its size (the discarded partial). Doubling: pages: 200,400,800,1600,3200,4096,4096... capped at 4096 records/page ≈ 4MB. So ~12-15 pages, each reading a strip of size blockBytes (capped by maxBytes too — defaultChunkBytes?).

What's defaultChunkBytes? If defaultChunkBytes = 512KB then blockBytes doubles 512K→1M→2M→4M→8M→16M→32M→64M: total read ≈ 127MB for a 32.5MB file → 4× read amplification, PLUS each strip's parse. And each page also re-reads/re-parses the discarded older segment? No — next page anchors at the kept-first's offset, so each byte is read... wait: strip [top-span, top). Keep newest 200 records → firstOffset = offset of the 200th-newest record in the strip. Next page reads [firstOffset - span', firstOffset). So no re-read; the discarded older portion of the strip is NEVER read again (the next strip covers it). Hmm, so each byte read once. Total ≈ 32.5MB.

BUT: the per-record cap at 200/400/.../4096 means per-page `_parseAllLines` parses the WHOLE strip (span bytes, up to 64MB... no wait — strip is maxBytes=blockBytes AND records capped after parse. Parse cost = strip size. Total parse ≈ file size. Read total: strips double: 512K+1M+2M+...+32M = 64MB-ish. So ~2× read+parse amplification ≈ 1.6-1.7s? Close to the observed 3.3s maybe with JIT variance. And the full open reads exactly 32.5MB once.

So the fix for the walk: start with BIGGER initial blocks. growOlderUntil starts at `_chunkRecords/_chunkBytes` (the interactive chunk size — small, for UI paging) and doubles per page. For a whole-ledger walk that's read-amplifying: sum of doubling geometric series ≈ 2× file. Plus per-page strip re-split.

Options:
a) In `ensureWholeLedgerResident`, call growOlderUntil with larger starting block? The start sizes are internal (`_chunkRecords`, `_chunkBytes` fields). Add optional `initialBlockRecords`/`initialBlockBytes` params to growOlderUntil, and have ensureWholeLedgerResident pass maxWalkBlockRecords/maxWalkBlockBytes directly (a single 64MB strip per page, no doubling ramp). Pages: ceil(32.5MB/64MB)=1 page + tail... blockRecords cap 4096: 30k records need 8 pages of 4096. Each page reads ≤64MB strip... strips: 32MB last... total read ≈ 32.5MB × ~1.0-1.5.

Actually with blockBytes=64MB and blockRecords=4096 from the start: page strips: readBlockBefore reads strip of 64MB → capped at 4096 records (sublist keeps newest 4096 → ~4MB) — WASTEFUL: it reads a 64MB strip to keep 4MB! The maxRecords cap makes big strips useless. Better: size the strip to the RECORD cap: bytes-per-record average... The reader doesn't know record sizes ahead.

Hmm — actually rethink: for whole-ledger walk, the natural primitive is the STREAMED SCAN (like the full open's SessionLineScanner): read sequentially from the file head in bounded chunks, parse incrementally, append to index. That's exactly what `_openStreamedLocked` does. But records arrive oldest-first while the windowed index needs... appending oldest-first at the HEAD — order doesn't matter for maps, but `_entries` must stay file-ordered — prepending oldest-first = repeated insertAll(0, chunk) per page → O(total²/page_size)... with insertAll(0, list) each page costs O(window) memmove — total O(N²/page) — no good for big N with many pages. Could collect pages and build the final list once — but intermediate pages... We could accumulate parsed pages in a list-of-pages and only splice into _entries ONCE at the end. But _entries feeds getPathToRoot during the walk (the loop needs branch each iteration for found/budget checks — but with found=(_)=>false and tokenBudget=null, the per-page branch check is `branch.any(found) && ...` → false always; and `if (!_hasOlder) return true`. messages.preview: My slot math reversed the list (side-effect order ≠ list order). Fix:

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

blocks.text:
The walk itself is 3291ms. The full open does the equivalent read+parse in ~800ms. So per-page work has ~2.5s of extra. What differs per page?

Full open streamed scan (`_openStreamedLocked`): SessionLineScanner over ranges, parse via `_parseExecutor`? No — check how full open parses: maybe it uses the parseExecutor pool when available... none here. Let me look at what readBlockBefore does vs the streamed scan:

1. `_readStripLines(limit, maxBytes)`: span starts at maxBytes. What is defaultChunkBytes? Let me check — maybe 256KB. span doubles until a complete line fits. Each iteration reads [limit-span, limit). Normally 1 iteration.
2. `_splitLines(bytes, lo)` — scan for \n.
3. `_parseAllLines(lines)` — parse each line.

Hypothesis: `_parseAllLines` runs on the `parseExecutor`... if null, inline. Same as scanner.

What about JSON decode: line bytes → utf8 decode → jsonDecode → SessionRecord.fromJson? The streamed scan may use a FASTER shallow/deferred parse? Actually! I remember session_storage streamed open has "shallow-parse header extraction"... no.

Alternatively the walk's `getPathToRoot(leaf)` + `_keptPathResident` per page... O(N) small.

Hmm — what about `_readOlderBlock`'s `chunk.entries.length` — with maxRecords: 200 → blockRecords starts at _chunkRecords = 200 records?? WAIT. Look at growOlderUntil: `var blockRecords = _chunkRecords; var blockBytes = _chunkBytes;` then per page `blockRecords *= 2` capped at maxWalkBlockRecords=4096, blockBytes capped at 64MB. But `readBlockBefore(top, maxRecords: blockRecords, maxBytes: blockBytes)` — the strip is capped by BOTH: entries.length > maxRecords → sublist keeps the NEWEST maxRecords of the strip and sets hasOlder=true... 

CRITICAL BUG (perf): if maxRecords caps the block (e.g., blockRecords=200 for page 1), the entries BELOW the kept 200 (older ones in the same strip) are DISCARDED but `_windowTopOffset = chunk.firstOffset` advances only to the first KEPT entry's offset — the older discarded part of the strip is re-read on the next page! With records ~1KB each: 200 records ≈ 200KB per page. 32.5MB / 200KB = 160 pages! Each page re-reads + re-parses the strip up to 2× its size (the discarded partial). Doubling: pages: 200,400,800,1600,3200,4096,4096... capped at 4096 records/page ≈ 4MB. So ~12-15 pages, each reading a strip of size blockBytes (capped by maxBytes too — defaultChunkBytes?).

What's defaultChunkBytes? If defaultChunkBytes = 512KB then blockBytes doubles 512K→1M→2M→4M→8M→16M→32M→64M: total read ≈ 127MB for a 32.5MB file → 4× read amplification, PLUS each strip's parse. And each page also re-reads/re-parses the discarded older segment? No — next page anchors at the kept-first's offset, so each byte is read... wait: strip [top-span, top). Keep newest 200 records → firstOffset = offset of the 200th-newest record in the strip. Next page reads [firstOffset - span', firstOffset). So no re-read; the discarded older portion of the strip is NEVER read again (the next strip covers it). Hmm, so each byte read once. Total ≈ 32.5MB.

BUT: the per-record cap at 200/400/.../4096 means per-page `_parseAllLines` parses the WHOLE strip (span bytes, up to 64MB... no wait — strip is maxBytes=blockBytes AND records capped after parse. Parse cost = strip size. Total parse ≈ file size. Read total: strips double: 512K+1M+2M+...+32M = 64MB-ish. So ~2× read+parse amplification ≈ 1.6-1.7s? Close to the observed 3.3s maybe with JIT variance. And the full open reads exactly 32.5MB once.

So the fix for the walk: start with BIGGER initial blocks. growOlderUntil starts at `_chunkRecords/_chunkBytes` (the interactive chunk size — small, for UI paging) and doubles per page. For a whole-ledger walk that's read-amplifying: sum of doubling geometric series ≈ 2× file. Plus per-page strip re-split.

Options:
a) In `ensureWholeLedgerResident`, call growOlderUntil with larger starting block? The start sizes are internal (`_chunkRecords`, `_chunkBytes` fields). Add optional `initialBlockRecords`/`initialBlockBytes` params to growOlderUntil, and have ensureWholeLedgerResident pass maxWalkBlockRecords/maxWalkBlockBytes directly (a single 64MB strip per page, no doubling ramp). Pages: ceil(32.5MB/64MB)=1 page + tail... blockRecords cap 4096: 30k records need 8 pages of 4096. Each page reads ≤64MB strip... strips: 32MB last... total read ≈ 32.5MB × ~1.0-1.5.

Actually with blockBytes=64MB and blockRecords=4096 from the start: page strips: readBlockBefore reads strip of 64MB → capped at 4096 records (sublist keeps newest 4096 → ~4MB) — WASTEFUL: it reads a 64MB strip to keep 4MB! The maxRecords cap makes big strips useless. Better: size the strip to the RECORD cap: bytes-per-record average... The reader doesn't know record sizes ahead.

Hmm — actually rethink: for whole-ledger walk, the natural primitive is the STREAMED SCAN (like the full open's SessionLineScanner): read sequentially from the file head in bounded chunks, parse incrementally, append to index. That's exactly what `_openStreamedLocked` does. But records arrive oldest-first while the windowed index needs... appending oldest-first at the HEAD — order doesn't matter for maps, but `_entries` must stay file-ordered — prepending oldest-first = repeated insertAll(0, chunk) per page → O(total²/page_size)... with insertAll(0, list) each page costs O(window) memmove — total O(N²/page) — no good for big N with many pages. Could collect pages and build the final list once — but intermediate pages... We could accumulate parsed pages in a list-of-pages and only splice into _entries ONCE at the end. But _entries feeds getPathToRoot during the walk (the loop needs branch each iteration for found/budget checks — but with found=(_)=>false and tokenBudget=null, the per-page branch check is `branch.any(found) && ...` → false always; and `if (!_hasOlder) return true`. And `_keptPathResident`? Only checked when found matches. So for ensureWholeLedgerResident the per-page branch recompute is useless work — but growOlderUntil is shared.

Pragmatic approach: keep growOlderUntil but make the block sizing smarter for deep walks:
- The real cost issue: doubling from small start reads ~2× and parses ~2×, plus per-page strip overhead. 2× of 819ms ≈ 1.6s, observed 3.3s. There's more: per page, `readBlockBefore` ALSO stats the file (`await stat()`), `_readStripLines` may double spans for line alignment (each page: the strip's first line is partial → discarded — with 4MB strips, tiny waste).

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073

  activation (W2), and the opt-in write-side caps (W3) remain follow-up
  work.

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

messages.preview: My slot math reversed the list (side-effect order ≠ list order). Fix:

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

messages.preview: My slot math reversed the list (side-effect order ≠ list order). Fix:

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

messages.preview: My slot math reversed the list (side-effect order ≠ list order). Fix:

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

{"newText":"- gh-1555 (W1, lazy/windowed-everywhere reads): the legacy full-open call
  sites migrate to windowed opens, so a session ledger past the gh-1073
  2 GiB full-open backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path.
  The TUI session picker, `/resume`, and the boot name-resolution scan
  open windowed and resolve the display name through paged reads; the
  subagent transcript preview opens the child windowed (tail only); the
  `_loadSession` marathon fallback no longer degenerates to a refused
  full open when the boundary walk exhausts its page cap (it proceeds
  with the tail-anchored windowed session; the boot cap owns over-window
  residue); and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver opens windowed,
  reading the whole ledger for the cost/inspect views through the new
  `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident` — a sequential forward scan in
  bounded strips (`WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder`), not the
  boundary-walk's doubling strips (whose per-strip record cap measured
  ~13x read/parse amplification over the whole file). The same change

messages.preview: My slot math reversed the list (side-effect order ≠ list order). Fix:

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

messages.preview: My slot math reversed the list (side-effect order ≠ list order). Fix:

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

messages.preview: My slot math reversed the list (side-effect order ≠ list order). Fix:

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

messages.preview: My slot math reversed the list (side-effect order ≠ list order). Fix:

blocks.text:
My `_indexChunk` rewrite broke prepend ordering! The actual list is REVERSED. Let me re-check my slot logic.

Old loop: `for (i = first = n-1; i >= 0; i--)` — newest-first, each `insert(0)`. So for chunk entries [c0(oldest), c1, ..., c(n-1)(newest)]: iteration i=n-1 first → insert c(n-1) at 0 → [c(n-1)]. Then i=n-2 → insert at 0 → [c(n-2), c(n-1)]. Final: [c0, c1, ..., c(n-1)] — file order at head. Correct.

My version: `slot = n - 1 - i`. i=0 (oldest) → slot = n-1 → records[n-1] = c0. i=n-1 (newest) → slot=0 → records[0] = c(n-1). So records = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — REVERSED! Then insertAll(0, records) → window head = [c(n-1), ..., c0] — reversed. BUG: slot should be `i`, not `n-1-i`. I confused myself: the side-effect ORDER (newest-first) differs from the LIST ORDER (file order). The list build should just use slot=i (file order); only the map side-effects loop order mattered (and that order is irrelevant — map writes commute). Fix: slot = i.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

1. **Picker** (`_tuiPickSession`): open `windowed: true`. The picker only needs `getSessionName()` + metadata. Need to check getSessionName works on windowed storage — it reads session_info records; windowed materializes header+newest chunk, name record is usually near tail. Also `_switchToMetadata` presumably calls `_loadSession`, which opens windowed anyway. Good.

2. **`_resumeLastSession`**: open `windowed: true` (only needs name + then `_switchToMetadata`).

3. **`_openChildSession`**: open `windowed: true` (needs only last 8 messages — tail resident).

4. **`_loadSession` marathon fallback**: currently `session = await _repo.open(metadata)` full open when `ensureCompactionBoundaryResident` returns false. Change to: keep the windowed session (log diagnostic). But wait — false means maxPages exhaustion during walk (512 pages, doubling blocks capped at 64MB/4096 records — that's astronomically large; ~512×64MB = 32GB). In practice false means a genuinely enormous/degenerate session. Ticket says fallback should page by token budget — which the walk already does. So replacing the full-open fallback with "proceed with the tail-resident windowed session" is the right change. Actually wait — there's a subtlety: AC9 meter continuity and "boundary-less marathon must tail-read the last N tokens, not full-open". The walk with tokenBudget already does that and returns true. The full-open fallback only triggers on maxPages exhaustion. Replacing it with proceed-as-windowed keeps memory bounded. 

5. **`resolveTrajectorySession`** + headless `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` + `agent_hub_cli.dart:257`: The trajectory view/tail only need the tail; cost needs the whole session cumulative (requests cumulativeUsage — snapshot.requests from the whole branch). TrajectorySnapshotBuilder is incremental and cheap per record (projection), but `getBranch()` on full-open materializes everything in memory — the memory hog. Windowed `getBranch()` returns only resident records (tail window). For `view`/`tail` the tail is fine (maxLines=200 cap anyway; but index numbers/“earlier hidden” count would change...). Hmm — changing to windowed would change outputs for deep sessions (record indexes relative to tail only, cost table incomplete). That changes behavior for sessions > window. For sessions below the window, windowed materializes everything → identical output (AC7).

   This is where it gets tricky. The honest W1 approach for `fa trajectory view/tail`: windowed is acceptable since view is capped at 200 lines from the tail anyway. For `cost`: needs full history — can't lie. For a marathon session, cost over windowed tail gives partial numbers. Option: page the whole branch through the windowed storage in bounded blocks (growOlderUntil-style walk to file head), feeding the incremental builder — memory bounded by the snapshot size itself (the projection). The trajectory snapshot is much smaller than raw records, but for a 100GB ledger even the snapshot could be big. Still, bounded by projected size, not raw size.
